items.title: Polymarket moves Protocol V2 launch to November 9, after its original November 2 target, Bitrue reports
items.body: - **Polymarket moves Protocol V2 launch to November 9, after its original November 2 target, Bitrue reports** — Bitrue reports Polymarket is preparing to launch Protocol V2 on November 9, 2026, replacing its legacy Gnosis-based infrastructure with unified smart contracts and pUSD, a standard ERC-20 collateral token on Polygon. V1 orders and SDKs are not compatible with V2, so automated trading systems will need to migrate. (Bitrue)

items.title: DraftKings cuts 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to 175 million to 275 million dollars from 700 million to 900 million dollars as prediction market spending rises, TradersUnion reports
items.body: - **DraftKings cuts 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to 175 million to 275 million dollars from 700 million to 900 million dollars as prediction market spending rises, TradersUnion reports** — TradersUnion reports DraftKings lowered its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to 175 million to 275 million dollars, from 700 million to 900 million dollars, citing up to 700 million dollars in prediction market investment. Its new 2027 adjusted EBITDA forecast of 800 million to 1 billion dollars also fell short of Bloomberg consensus of about 1.1 billion dollars. (TradersUnion)

items.title: Five of ten prediction market firms have complied with Ohio cease-and-desist orders on sports contracts, with Coinbase set to stop on November 13, WiseVoter reports
items.body: - **Five of ten prediction market firms have complied with Ohio cease-and-desist orders on sports contracts, with Coinbase set to stop on November 13, WiseVoter reports** — WiseVoter reports MooMoo Financial, Robinhood and Gemini no longer offer new sports event contracts in Ohio and Plus500US was in compliance as of October 21, after the Ohio Casino Control Commission sent cease-and-desist orders to 10 prediction markets and brokers on October 2. Polymarket and Underdog have filed lawsuits against the commission, Coinbase will stop offering the contracts in Ohio on November 13, and the commission remains in discussions with three other companies. (WiseVoter)

items.title: Kalshi parlay taker losses top 1 billion dollars since the product launched in September 2025, InGame reports
items.body: - **Kalshi parlay taker losses top 1 billion dollars since the product launched in September 2025, InGame reports** — InGame analysis shows Kalshi multi-leg parlay volume has reached 165.6 billion dollars since September 2025, with taker stakes of 7.1 billion dollars and taker losses of 1.004 billion dollars, including about 400 million dollars in fees. items.title: CFTC directs prediction market exchanges to end domestic geographic restrictions within 30 days, NJToday reports
items.body: - **CFTC directs prediction market exchanges to end domestic geographic restrictions within 30 days, NJToday reports** — The CFTC has issued an interpretation directing designated contract markets and prediction market platforms to cease domestic geographic restrictions within 30 days or explain why compliance is not feasible, citing impartial access requirements under Regulation 38.151(b). The directive leaves platforms such as Kalshi caught between federal requirements for national access and state court orders demanding regional geofencing. (NJToday)

items.title: War and violent event contracts are banned on Kalshi under the CFTC public interest rule while Polymarket's international exchange lists them, Best Predictions reports
items.body: - **War and violent event contracts are banned on Kalshi under the CFTC public interest rule while Polymarket's international exchange lists them, Best Predictions reports** — Best Predictions' November rundown says CFTC Regulation 40.11 bars registered exchanges from listing contracts involving terrorism, assassination, war, gaming or unlawful activity, and Kalshi's own policy bans violent markets including war and kidnapping. The CFTC proposed case-by-case review in June 2026 and comments closed in July, but no final rule had been published as of November 5, 2026, so the ban stands on regulated US exchanges. (Best Predictions)

items.title: South Carolina Democrat Annie Andrews beats Republican Darline Graham, who had been favored at about 70 percent in market odds, in the first prediction market upset of the night, Reuters reports

items.title: Appeals courts split over whether sports event contracts are swaps, putting prediction market regulation on a road to the Supreme Court, Foley and Lardner reports
items.body: - **Appeals courts split over whether sports event contracts are swaps, putting prediction market regulation on a road to the Supreme Court, Foley and Lardner reports** — Foley and Lardner reports federal appellate courts are divided on whether prediction market contracts are federally regulated derivatives or state-regulated gambling, with the Third Circuit backing Kalshi on preemption in New Jersey while the Ninth Circuit reached the opposite conclusion and the Sixth Circuit joined the Ninth on September 25 in cases from Ohio and Tennessee. Kalshi filed a petition for rehearing en banc in the Sixth Circuit on October 9, and multiple parties have filed petitions asking the Supreme Court to resolve the split. (Foley & Lardner)

items.body: - **Prediction market litigation is split across three appeals courts, with the Third Circuit backing Kalshi against New Jersey while the Ninth and Sixth Circuits side with the states, Foley and Lardner reports** — Foley and Lardner says federal appeals courts are divided on whether sports event contracts are swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act: the Third Circuit affirmed a preliminary injunction against New Jersey in KalshiEX v. items.title: Kalshi House and Senate control contracts traded over 420 million dollars in notional volume as of November 3, Bloomberg data via Multibagg reports
items.body: - **Kalshi House and Senate control contracts traded over 420 million dollars in notional volume as of November 3, Bloomberg data via Multibagg reports** — Multibagg, citing Bloomberg, reports the Kalshi congressional control volume split was 247 million dollars for the House and 177 million dollars for the Senate as of 11:30 a.m. ET on November 3. It also cites Anti-Corruption Data Collective data showing the top 1 percent of Polymarket Global wallets made up 68 percent of congressional-market volume through August 10, and a Vanderbilt study scoring PredictIt at 93 percent, Kalshi at 78 percent and Polymarket at 67 percent across about 2,500 markets in the final five weeks of 2024. (Multibagg)

items.title: Kalshi election-market volume topped 2.5 billion dollars this cycle, up from 1.3 billion in 2024, and Polymarket forecasts were about 98 percent accurate, Reuters via DevDiscourse reports
items.body: - **Kalshi election-market volume topped 2.5 billion dollars this cycle, up from 1.3 billion in 2024, and Polymarket forecasts were about 98 percent accurate, Reuters via DevDiscourse reports** — DevDiscourse, citing Reuters, reports Kalshi's total trading volume on election markets reached over 2.5 billion dollars this cycle, compared with 1.3 billion dollars during the 2024 cycle that included the presidential race, while a person familiar with the matter put Polymarket's election forecast accuracy at about 98 percent. One notable miss came in South Carolina, where Democrat Annie Andrews defeated Republican Darline Graham despite markets implying about a 70 percent chance for Graham late on Tuesday. (DevDiscourse)

items.title: Political betting was just 1 percent of Kalshi and Polymarket trading in October, down from two-thirds during the 2024 presidential election, Bloomberg data via ZeroHedge reports
items.body: - **Political betting was just 1 percent of Kalshi and Polymarket trading in October, down from two-thirds during the 2024 presidential election, Bloomberg data via ZeroHedge reports** — ZeroHedge, citing a Bloomberg report, says political betting on Kalshi and Polymarket accounted for just 1 percent of trading in October, down from two-thirds during the 2024 presidential election, even as overall trading across both platforms has increased more than twentyfold since October 2024. Election-related turnover on Kalshi was roughly unchanged in the final week before the midterms compared with the same period in 2024, while Polymarket's election volume fell significantly as sports and crypto trading boomed. (ZeroHedge)

The Miami Heat show the next widest gap in the same market, at 1 cent on Polymarket US against 7 cents on Gemini. (Rivo)

items.title: Stock futures rally after the Democratic sweep, with Nasdaq and S and P 500 futures each up 1.1 percent and the Dow up 1.5 percent, Morningstar reports
items.body: - **Stock futures rally after the Democratic sweep, with Nasdaq and S and P 500 futures each up 1.1 percent and the Dow up 1.5 percent, Morningstar reports** — Morningstar, via Dow Jones Newswires, reports United States stock futures reversed earlier losses on November 4 after Democrats won both chambers, with analysts citing relief that a balance of power would keep both parties in check. Brent crude fell 1.4 percent to about 102.20 dollars a barrel, gold rallied back above 4,000 dollars an ounce, and Bitcoin hovered around 78,400 dollars. (Morningstar)

items.body: - **Trump Media shares sank nearly 7 percent ahead of the opening bell after the midterm results, Morningstar reports** — Morningstar reports Trump Media and Technology shares fell nearly 7 percent in premarket trading on November 4 following the Democratic sweep of Congress. The same briefing said oil prices dropped as investors weighed the sweep's geopolitical implications, with Capital Economics warning Brent could rise above 120 dollars a barrel if strikes on Iran resume. (Morningstar)

items.title: Stablecoin market capitalization fell to about 263 billion dollars, its lowest level in more than a year, CryptoQuant data via Brave New Coin reports
items.body: - **Stablecoin market capitalization fell to about 263 billion dollars, its lowest level in more than a year, CryptoQuant data via Brave New Coin reports** — Brave New Coin reports CryptoQuant data showing total stablecoin market capitalization declined to approximately 263 billion dollars by early November 2026, signaling declining liquidity across cryptocurrency markets. Gold and silver also fell alongside risk assets ahead of the midterms as margin calls and forced deleveraging outweighed safe-haven demand, before recovering on November 2. (Brave New Coin)

items.title: Kalshi contracts that settle on VoteHub polling averages face scrutiny after Wedgewood admitted fabricating most of its surveys, iCoinMarket reports
items.body: - **Kalshi contracts that settle on VoteHub polling averages face scrutiny after Wedgewood admitted fabricating most of its surveys, iCoinMarket reports** — iCoinMarket reports polling firm Wedgewood acknowledged on October 20 that it had fabricated most of its election surveys, and VoteHub, an aggregator that carried those results, is the named data source for recurring Kalshi contracts. Kalshi's filing states revisions made after expiration will not be counted in determining the expiration value, raising questions about contracts settled on figures later withdrawn. (iCoinMarket)

items.title: Prediction markets score big as Democrats sweep Congress, with Polymarket sweep volume above 60 million dollars and Kalshi above 100 million, Seeking Alpha reports
items.body: - **Prediction markets score big as Democrats sweep Congress, with Polymarket sweep volume above 60 million dollars and Kalshi above 100 million, Seeking Alpha reports** — Seeking Alpha reports Polymarket and Kalshi both priced a Democratic sweep above 75 percent before Election Day, with sweep odds reaching 77 percent on Polymarket and about 75 percent on Kalshi in early Tuesday trading. Democrats ultimately captured both chambers, validating the shift in odds that built through the final weeks of the campaign. (Seeking Alpha)

items.title: CFTC says trading in single-stock perpetual futures can begin on registered commodity markets, Reuters reports

items.body: - **Kalshi can settle midterm contracts on a four-of-eight media consensus while Polymarket uses a two-hour UMA challenge window, Covers explains** — Covers explains that Kalshi midterm rules allow accelerated settlement when at least four of eight designated media sources declare the same winner with no contradictory call, with Senate control falling back to the president pro tempore's party on February 1, 2027 if there is no consensus. items.title: Study of 358,236 resolved markets finds favourites won 76.9 percent of the time, with Polymarket and Kalshi about equally accurate, PredictDesks reports
items.body: - **Study of 358,236 resolved markets finds favourites won 76.9 percent of the time, with Polymarket and Kalshi about equally accurate, PredictDesks reports** — PredictDesks reports its study of 358,236 resolved markets, 333,464 on Polymarket and 24,772 on Kalshi, found the favourite won 76.9 percent of the time across all markets and 92.8 percent a day out on long-running markets. Weighted to the same mix of topics, the two platforms' Brier scores were nearly identical at 0.150 for Polymarket and 0.147 for Kalshi, while ladder markets were overconfident, with outcomes priced under 10 cents winning 1.6 times as often as their price implied. (PredictDesks)

items.title: About 3 percent of accounts drive prediction market accuracy while 0.1 percent took three-quarters of the profits, Mogaz reports
items.body: - **About 3 percent of accounts drive prediction market accuracy while 0.1 percent took three-quarters of the profits, Mogaz reports** — Mogaz reports Judith Levine's critique that a working paper from London Business School and Yale scholars found almost every wagerer's results were no better than chance, with market accuracy coming from around 3 percent of accounts. It adds that three-quarters of the profits went to 0.1 percent of accounts, and that of at least 2.3 million Polymarket accounts, just 2,000 netted almost half a billion dollars. (Mogaz)

items.body: - **Kansas Senate is the biggest seven-day mover on Kalshi, jumping 24 points from 41 percent to 65 percent for Democrats, DeFi Rate reports** — DeFi Rate reports its biggest-moves board, using daily closes to its 5:04 p.m. ET observation, shows the Kansas Senate market up 24 points in seven days to 65 percent for Democrats on Kalshi. Texas Senate rose 9 points to 75 percent and Maine Senate rose 9 points to 70 percent over the same span. (DeFi Rate)

items.title: Kalshi has fined and suspended four congressional candidates this year for trading on their own races, RotoWire reports
items.body: - **Kalshi has fined and suspended four congressional candidates this year for trading on their own races, RotoWire reports** — RotoWire reports Kalshi prohibits candidates, congressional staff, campaign employees and media decision desks from trading on relevant election markets and has already fined and suspended four congressional candidates this year. Kalshi said less than 1 percent of its U.S. election trades come from foreign accounts, and its markets settle only after at least four of eight major news organizations call a race with no disagreement. (RotoWire)

items.title: Kalshi holds about 3.2 times Polymarket's midterm volume, at about 1.1 billion dollars against about 340 million, Trefis reports
items.body: - **Kalshi holds about 3.2 times Polymarket's midterm volume, at about 1.1 billion dollars against about 340 million, Trefis reports** — Trefis reports that as of about October 23, roughly 1.1 billion dollars had traded on Kalshi's 2026 midterm markets against about 340 million dollars on Polymarket, leaving the platform that led 2024 election night in second place this cycle. It notes Polymarket's volume fell 84 percent the morning after the 2024 election, with a smaller drop expected this time because the midterms are smaller than a presidential race. (Trefis)

items.body: - **House control average climbs to 96 percent for Democrats in the early evening read, with Polymarket at 96.8 cents against Kalshi at 95.4 cents, DeFi Rate reports** — DeFi Rate reports its House control page, observed between 5:56 p.m. and 6:26 p.m. ET, averages Democrats at 96 percent across Kalshi at 95.4 cents, Polymarket at 96.8 cents and Polymarket US at 96.3 cents, up from a 93.9 percent average earlier in the evening. Its balance of power board averages a Democratic sweep at 78 percent, built from a wide venue split of Kalshi at 74.5 cents and Polymarket at 80.5 cents. (DeFi Rate)

items.title: Cboe floor read puts the Senate at 78 percent for Democrats, up about 11 points in the last week, with a sweep at 77 percent, Fintech TV reports
items.body: - **Cboe floor read puts the Senate at 78 percent for Democrats, up about 11 points in the last week, with a sweep at 77 percent, Fintech TV reports** — Fintech TV reports contributor Errol Coleman, speaking from the Cboe trading floor on Election Day, put prediction market pricing at about 95 percent for Democrats to win the House and about 78 percent for the Senate, with a Democratic sweep of both chambers at about 77 percent. Coleman noted Senate expectations had risen by about 11 percent over the last week as the midterms got closer. (Fintech TV)

items.title: JPMorgan runs below the prediction markets on a blue wave, at 66 percent against market sweep pricing near 75 percent, The Evergreen Edit reports
items.body: - **JPMorgan runs below the prediction markets on a blue wave, at 66 percent against market sweep pricing near 75 percent, The Evergreen Edit reports** — The Evergreen Edit reports JPMorgan, via CNBC, assigned 66 percent to Democrats winning both chambers, 26 percent to a Democratic House with a Republican Senate, 7 percent to Republicans keeping both chambers and 1 percent to a Republican House with a Democratic Senate. The bank's 66 percent sweep figure sits well below the roughly 75 to 78 percent sweep pricing on Kalshi and Polymarket, and JPMorgan estimated the S&P 500 reaction to a sweep at between a 0.25 percent dip and a 0.50 percent gain. (The Evergreen Edit)

items.title: Bearish election posts hit their highest level in a month as crypto traders watch Polymarket price a Democratic sweep at 74 percent, BeInCrypto reports
items.body: - **Bearish election posts hit their highest level in a month as crypto traders watch Polymarket price a Democratic sweep at 74 percent, BeInCrypto reports** — BeInCrypto reports analytics firm Santiment counted its highest level of bearish election posts in a month of tracked social data as Polymarket priced a Democratic sweep of both chambers at 74 percent. It notes Polymarket also gives 81 percent odds that the Associated Press calls the House by the end of Wednesday, while Bitcoin traded near 77,768 dollars, up 0.2 percent in 24 hours. (BeInCrypto)

items.title: Kalshi's House control market is its most heavily traded midterm market, at about 157 million dollars traded since opening at 76 percent in May, OddsChecker reports
items.body: - **Kalshi's House control market is its most heavily traded midterm market, at about 157 million dollars traded since opening at 76 percent in May, OddsChecker reports** — OddsChecker reports Kalshi's House control market opened on May 27 with Democrats at 76 percent and had become the most heavily traded midterm market on Kalshi, with about 157 million dollars traded as of October 28. It puts Democrats at about 94 percent on Kalshi and 95 percent on Polymarket for the House on Election Day, with a Democratic sweep of both chambers the single most likely outcome at around 75 percent. (OddsChecker)

items.title: Senate markets barely flinch at the first exit polls, with Kalshi Senate control dipping just 1 point to 73 percent for Democrats, The Prediction Network reports
items.body: - **Senate markets barely flinch at the first exit polls, with Kalshi Senate control dipping just 1 point to 73 percent for Democrats, The Prediction Network reports** — The Prediction Network reports in its 5:30 p.m. ET update that Senate race prices held where they were at 4:30 p.m. ET after the first exit polls showed President Trump at 38 percent approval, with Texas the most traded race as James Talarico held about 73 percent on more than 92 million dollars traded. (The Prediction Network)

items.title: Senate control averages 74.8 percent for Democrats at 6:09 p.m. ET, with Kalshi's 74.1 percent constructed from its balance of power legs against Polymarket at 75.5 percent, DeFi Rate reports
items.body: - **Senate control averages 74.8 percent for Democrats at 6:09 p.m. ET, with Kalshi's 74.1 percent constructed from its balance of power legs against Polymarket at 75.5 percent, DeFi Rate reports** — DeFi Rate explains in its sources page, observed at 6:09 p.m. ET, that Kalshi lists no single Senate control contract, so its price is built by adding the two balance of power outcomes in which Democrats win the Senate, at 73.5 cents and 0.55 cents. Its House average is 93.9 percent, from Kalshi at 93.25 percent and Polymarket at 94.5 percent. (DeFi Rate)

items.title: Historical research finds prediction markets have overstated the challenging party's sweep odds at this point in the last five midterms, ZeroHedge reports
items.body: - **Historical research finds prediction markets have overstated the challenging party's sweep odds at this point in the last five midterms, ZeroHedge reports** — ZeroHedge reports Goldman Sachs told clients the Democratic House looks priced as done, with Polymarket at 96 percent, leaving the Senate as the only real source of election night surprise. It cites research by Phillips finding markets tended to overstate sweep odds in the five previous midterms back to 2002, and notes an ACA beneficiaries basket tracked Kalshi sweep odds almost tick for tick since summer until diverging in the last two weeks. (ZeroHedge)

items.title: Nate Silver's FLIPR model gives Democrats polling leads of 4.9 points in Michigan, 3.9 in Maine, 3.3 in Texas, 3 in Ohio and 1.1 in Iowa, Coinpedia reports
items.body: - **Nate Silver's FLIPR model gives Democrats polling leads of 4.9 points in Michigan, 3.9 in Maine, 3.3 in Texas, 3 in Ohio and 1.1 in Iowa, Coinpedia reports** — Coinpedia reports in its live midterm coverage that the FLIPR model's November 3 update calls a Democratic House majority close to certain and favours Democrats for the Senate, with its closest lead in Iowa at 1.1 points. The figures are polling averages rather than market prices, setting up a direct model against market comparison as Senate results arrive tonight. (Coinpedia)

items.body: - **Prediction market odds put Democrats at about 95 percent for the House and 75 percent for the Senate as Wall Street trades into the results, XTB reports** — XTB reports the S&P 500 rose about 0.5 percent and the Nasdaq 100 about 0.9 percent on Election Day while traders watched prediction market odds for chamber control. It notes that across the last 19 election cycles the S&P 500 was never negative 120 trading days after the election, averaging a gain of about 13 percent. (XTB)

items.title: Midterm election wagering passes 1.48 billion dollars as prediction markets face their biggest forecasting test, Reuters reports
items.body: - **Midterm election wagering passes 1.48 billion dollars as prediction markets face their biggest forecasting test, Reuters reports** — Reuters reports more than 1.48 billion dollars has been wagered on the midterms, with Kalshi reporting 1.33 billion dollars in midterm volume and about 145 million dollars on Polymarket congressional markets across more than 28,000 markets. The platforms face scrutiny over candidates betting on their own races and research finding political markets can be shifted with relatively small bets. (Reuters)

items.title: Kalshi governor odds diverge from its Senate trend, favouring Democrats in four of five governor races in states Trump won, Prediction News reports
items.body: - **Kalshi governor odds diverge from its Senate trend, favouring Democrats in four of five governor races in states Trump won, Prediction News reports** — Kalshi governor pricing favours Democrats in four of five governor races in states Trump won, including Georgia and Pennsylvania, running counter to the platform's Election Day Senate trend after Texas, Iowa, Michigan and Maine shifted Republican. The split sets up a live test of whether the same exchange can track divergent statehouse and Senate electorates at once. (Prediction News)

items.title: Senate control venue gap widens as Kalshi prices Democrats at 69 percent against 73 percent on Polymarket, Action Network reports
items.body: - **Senate control venue gap widens as Kalshi prices Democrats at 69 percent against 73 percent on Polymarket, Action Network reports** — Action Network reports Kalshi prices Democratic Senate control at 69 percent with the House at 91 percent, while Polymarket prices Senate control closer to 73 percent. Forecaster Nate Silver runs above both venues, at 95 percent for the House and in the high 70s for the Senate, while the Cook Political Report counts seven Senate races still within the margin of error. (Action Network)

items.title: AI forecaster Sikt runs below the markets on both chambers, with its widest gap in Ohio where it prices Sherrod Brown 12 points under the market, Sikt Intelligence reports
items.body: - **AI forecaster Sikt runs below the markets on both chambers, with its widest gap in Ohio where it prices Sherrod Brown 12 points under the market, Sikt Intelligence reports** — Sikt Intelligence prices Democratic House control at 91 percent and Senate control at 75 percent, below Kalshi and Polymarket at 94 percent and 76 to 78 percent. Its largest disagreement with the markets is Ohio, where it gives Sherrod Brown 60 percent against a market average near 72 percent, and every forecast will be graded against the results. (Sikt Intelligence)

items.title: Florida Senate market prices Ashley Moody at 88 cents on both exchanges, well above polling leads of 2 to 7 points over Angie Nixon, Action Network reports
items.body: - **Florida Senate market prices Ashley Moody at 88 cents on both exchanges, well above polling leads of 2 to 7 points over Angie Nixon, Action Network reports** — Polymarket and Kalshi both price Ashley Moody at 88 cents in the Florida Senate race against Angie Nixon at 14 cents on Polymarket, even though closing polls put Moody ahead by only 2 to 7 points. Both winner markets settle on the November 3 result, with polls closing at 7 p.m. ET. (Action Network)

items.title: Democratic sweep odds settle at 73 percent on Kalshi at 4:50 p.m. ET after hitting an all-time high of 75.6 percent earlier on Election Day, Kalshi News reports
items.body: - **Democratic sweep odds settle at 73 percent on Kalshi at 4:50 p.m. ET after hitting an all-time high of 75.6 percent earlier on Election Day, Kalshi News reports** — Kalshi News reports the sweep price climbed from 62.4 percent a week ago to the 75.6 percent high before easing to 73 percent at 4:50 p.m. ET, with a Democratic House and Republican Senate at 22 percent and a Republican sweep at 6.7 percent. Its separate chamber markets price Democrats at 93.6 percent for the House and 74 percent for the Senate, with Iowa's Senate race tied at 50 percent. (Kalshi News)

items.title: Kalshi and Polymarket give no public answers by Election Day to senators' election insider trading questions, Gaming America reports
items.body: - **Kalshi and Polymarket give no public answers by Election Day to senators' election insider trading questions, Gaming America reports** — Gaming America reports neither platform had published an answer on November 3 to the October 28 letter from Senators Warren and Curtis, which asked for counts of suspected insider trading and manipulation cases in election contracts identified, stopped before a trade, caught afterward and referred to the CFTC since January 1, 2026. Polymarket told the outlet it monitors election activity and refers suspicious traders to the Justice Department and the CFTC, while Kalshi did not respond to a request for comment by publication. (Gaming America)

items.title: Iowa Senate market sits at an even 50 cents on Kalshi at 3:46 p.m. ET, the only one of nine deciding races priced at even money, PredictionMarketPicks reports
items.body: - **Iowa Senate market sits at an even 50 cents on Kalshi at 3:46 p.m. ET, the only one of nine deciding races priced at even money, PredictionMarketPicks reports** — PredictionMarketPicks reports in its election night live coverage that the Iowa Democratic price was 50 cents at 3:46 p.m. ET, down from a fall high of 53 cents at 11 p.m. on Monday, with about 2.7 million Democratic and 3.5 million Republican contracts open. Its 3:52 p.m. ET chamber snapshot had Kalshi Senate control at 72 percent for Democrats and House control at 92 percent. (PredictionMarketPicks)

items.title: Maine Senate market eases to 69 percent for Troy Jackson on both venues, with Susan Collins priced 6 points apart at 33 percent on Polymarket and 27 percent on Kalshi, VegasInsider reports
items.body: - **Maine Senate market eases to 69 percent for Troy Jackson on both venues, with Susan Collins priced 6 points apart at 33 percent on Polymarket and 27 percent on Kalshi, VegasInsider reports** — VegasInsider reports in its November 3 update at 1:43 p.m. ET that Jackson holds 69 cents on both Polymarket and Kalshi ahead of Maine's 8 p.m. ET poll close, while the exchanges disagree on Collins as she chases a sixth term. Kalshi adds a Democratic margin forecast of 3.4 points for the race. (VegasInsider)

items.body: - **Senate control odds drift back toward Republicans in afternoon trading, with Democrats down to 73 percent from a 77 percent morning high while House control holds near 93 percent on Kalshi, InvestingLive reports** — InvestingLive reports the Senate control price eased from a 77 percent morning high-water mark to 73 percent in afternoon trading, compared with 74 percent at the same time on Monday, while House control was largely unchanged at about 93 percent for Democrats on Kalshi. Among the early-reporting districts to watch tonight, Kentucky's 7th district prices Democrat Zach Dembo at 59 percent after the Republican won the seat by 15 points in 2024. (InvestingLive)

items.title: Indiana secretary of state market flips twice on Election Day, with Democrat Beau Bayh back in front at 63 percent over Republican Max Engling at 34 percent on Kalshi at 3 p.m., IndyStar reports
items.body: - **Indiana secretary of state market flips twice on Election Day, with Democrat Beau Bayh back in front at 63 percent over Republican Max Engling at 34 percent on Kalshi at 3 p.m., IndyStar reports** — IndyStar reports Bayh led the Kalshi Indiana secretary of state market at 63 percent to Engling's 34 percent at 3 p.m. on Tuesday, after Engling briefly moved ahead around noon at 54.2 percent to 47.6 percent and Bayh had led 56 percent to 46 percent at 8 a.m. A recent Free Press Indiana poll also put Bayh ahead, at 43 percent to Engling's 35 percent, with 11 percent undecided. (IndyStar)

items.title: Los Angeles mayor market leans to incumbent Karen Bass at 58 percent over Nithya Raman at 43 percent on Kalshi, even though the final Berkeley poll had the two tied at 40 percent each, Covers reports
items.body: - **Los Angeles mayor market leans to incumbent Karen Bass at 58 percent over Nithya Raman at 43 percent on Kalshi, even though the final Berkeley poll had the two tied at 40 percent each, Covers reports** — Covers reports in its November 3 update at 1:32 p.m. ET that Kalshi prices Bass at 58 cents and Raman at 43 cents in the Los Angeles mayoral runoff, with about 109 million dollars traded on the market as of Election Day after the candidates traded the lead three times in October. A late-October Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies survey had the race tied at 40 percent each, with nearly one in five likely voters still undecided. (Covers)

items.title: Maine governor market is the state's lopsided race, with Democrat Hannah Pingree at 97 cents on Polymarket and 96.6 cents on Kalshi against Republican Bobby Charles ahead of the 8 p.m. poll close, Action Network reports
items.body: - **Maine governor market is the state's lopsided race, with Democrat Hannah Pingree at 97 cents on Polymarket and 96.6 cents on Kalshi against Republican Bobby Charles ahead of the 8 p.m. poll close, Action Network reports** — Action Network reports Kalshi's Maine governor margin forecast has Pingree ahead by 14.5 points, in line with the 11 to 12 point lead she held in the three most recent polls against Charles and independent Rick Bennett. Polls close in Maine at 8 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 3. (Action Network)

items.title: Georgia Senate market prices Jon Ossoff at 97 percent on Polymarket and 96 percent on Kalshi against Mike Collins in his reelection bid, RotoWire reports
items.body: - **Georgia Senate market prices Jon Ossoff at 97 percent on Polymarket and 96 percent on Kalshi against Mike Collins in his reelection bid, RotoWire reports** — RotoWire reports the consensus across Kalshi and Polymarket prices Ossoff at about 97 percent to hold his Georgia Senate seat, with Collins at 3 to 4 percent, and Kalshi's polling averages put Ossoff ahead by about 8.3 points. The Cook Political Report rates both the Georgia race and the open North Carolina seat as likely Democratic. (RotoWire)

items.title: Robinhood event contract revenue rises more than sixfold to 173 million dollars in the third quarter on a record 16.4 billion contracts traded, The Street reports
items.body: - **Robinhood event contract revenue rises more than sixfold to 173 million dollars in the third quarter on a record 16.4 billion contracts traded, The Street reports** — The Street reports Robinhood said third-quarter event contract revenue rose more than sixfold year over year to 173 million dollars, ahead of crypto revenue of 120 million dollars, as customers traded a record 16.4 billion event contracts, more than seven times the year-earlier count. Non-sports contracts, including elections, accounted for roughly 30 percent of prediction market activity, up from about 15 percent in the previous quarter, and Robinhood launched a dedicated U.S. Midterms Hub in September for congressional control and other election contracts. (The Street)

items.title: CFTC and Justice Department sue Utah to block state enforcement against Kalshi, their tenth state case and the first against a Republican-led state, SCCG reports
items.body: - **CFTC and Justice Department sue Utah to block state enforcement against Kalshi, their tenth state case and the first against a Republican-led state, SCCG reports** — SCCG reports the CFTC and the Department of Justice filed a 33-page federal complaint seeking to stop Utah Attorney General Derek Brown from applying state gambling restrictions, election betting prohibitions or public nuisance laws to CFTC-registered exchanges, after Utah sued Kalshi and two Susquehanna trading firms on October 20. Utah seeks to block contracts on sports, elections, politics and culture for state residents and estimates Kalshi collected between 30.6 million and 61.2 million dollars in fees from Utah accounts. (SCCG)

items.title: Kalshi adds a Ballotpedia-powered My Ballot guide to its Midterms Hub, as more than 80 percent of hub visitors use the platform for information without trading, Kalshi reports
items.body: - **Kalshi adds a Ballotpedia-powered My Ballot guide to its Midterms Hub, as more than 80 percent of hub visitors use the platform for information without trading, Kalshi reports** — Kalshi reports it launched My Ballot in its Midterms Hub using Ballotpedia's nonpartisan Sample Ballot Lookup data, matching each user's address to the Senate, House, governor, state legislative and ballot measure races on their ballot and pairing them with Kalshi market prices where an active market exists. Kalshi says more than 80 percent of Midterms Hub visitors do not trade and instead use the hub as part of their media diet, alongside Race Intel polling averages and FEC fundraising data from VoteHub. (Kalshi)

items.title: Turnout and party seat-total contracts trade alongside chamber control into the final hours of the midterms, Covers reports
items.body: - **Turnout and party seat-total contracts trade alongside chamber control into the final hours of the midterms, Covers reports** — Covers reports in its November 3 guide, updated at 12:26 p.m. ET, that beyond House and Senate control, traders can take positions on turnout through Kalshi's U.S. House turnout market and Polymarket US race props, where some contracts use vote-count ranges and others a threshold for a particular race. Party seat-total markets ask how many seats each party wins rather than simply who controls a chamber, and Covers notes turnout contracts are not necessarily a percentage of eligible voters. (Covers)

items.title: Intercontinental Exchange carries its Polymarket stake at about 2.0 billion dollars, roughly 22 percent of the platform's outstanding shares, PR Newswire reports
items.body: - **Intercontinental Exchange carries its Polymarket stake at about 2.0 billion dollars, roughly 22 percent of the platform's outstanding shares, PR Newswire reports** — PR Newswire reports Intercontinental Exchange, owner of the New York Stock Exchange, said in its third-quarter filing that the carrying value of its Series D and E preferred stock investments in Polymarket was approximately 2.0 billion dollars as of September 30, representing about 22 percent of Polymarket's outstanding shares and 14 percent on a fully diluted basis. ICE also completed a tender offer in April for approximately 0.4 million Polymarket common shares for 40 million dollars. (PR Newswire)

items.body: - **Virginia 5th district market jumps 23 points in 24 hours as Tom Perriello moves to 57 percent on Kalshi, PredictionBubbles reports** — PredictionBubbles reports its politics board, refreshed every 15 minutes, ranks the Kalshi market on a Democratic win in Virginia's 5th district, priced for Tom Perriello, as the biggest United States election mover of the last 24 hours, up 23 points to 57.0 percent on 841,000 dollars traded, reversing earlier pricing that favoured Republican incumbent John McGuire. items.title: Florida governor market trades at 3.9 times its daily average with 2.8 million dollars in 24 hours as Byron Donalds rises to 69 percent on Kalshi, DeFi Rate reports
items.body: - **Florida governor market trades at 3.9 times its daily average with 2.8 million dollars in 24 hours as Byron Donalds rises to 69 percent on Kalshi, DeFi Rate reports** — DeFi Rate reports its surging-markets list shows Kalshi's Florida governor winner market trading far above its usual pace on Election Day, at 3.9 times its daily average with 2.8 million dollars traded in 24 hours, with Byron Donalds leading at 69 percent, up from the 64 percent area where the market sat in late October. (DeFi Rate)

items.title: DraftKings promotes its new election markets with a paid Dave Portnoy post on election eve, offering 200 dollars in bonuses for a five dollar trade, The Comeback reports
items.body: - **DraftKings promotes its new election markets with a paid Dave Portnoy post on election eve, offering 200 dollars in bonuses for a five dollar trade, The Comeback reports** — The Comeback reports Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy posted a paid promotion with DraftKings on Monday for the company's DraftKings Predictions election markets, covering congressional seats, governor races and local campaigns through election night, with new customers offered 200 dollars in total bonuses for spending five dollars; DraftKings announced the Predictions app in December 2025. (The Comeback)

items.title: House control and balance of power markets pass 350 million dollars combined across 11 operators, Covers reports
items.body: - **House control and balance of power markets pass 350 million dollars combined across 11 operators, Covers reports** — Covers reports in its November 3 update at 4:03 p.m. ET that control of the House and the Congress balance of power markets have generated more than 350 million dollars combined in notional volume across 11 operators, according to Aldrin Research, with Polymarket volume led by Senate swing states Republicans will win at 67 million dollars and balance of power second at 65 million dollars. (Covers)

items.title: Polymarket swing-states market prices Republicans winning no Senate swing states as the likeliest outcome at 34 percent, Action Network reports
items.body: - **Polymarket swing-states market prices Republicans winning no Senate swing states as the likeliest outcome at 34 percent, Action Network reports** — Action Network reports Polymarket's market on which Senate swing states Republicans will win prices the None outcome, Republicans winning none of them, as the likeliest result at a 34 percent implied probability, down from 38 percent a day earlier, with Iowa the next outcome at 10 percent followed by an Iowa and Kansas combination bracket. (Action Network)

items.title: Markets price Democrats at 237 House seats and 53 or more Senate seats, with Republicans held under 185 House seats, Casino.org reports
items.body: - **Markets price Democrats at 237 House seats and 53 or more Senate seats, with Republicans held under 185 House seats, Casino.org reports** — Casino.org reports that as of midday trading on Election Day, prediction markets favour Democrats securing 53 or more Senate seats and winning 237 House seats, with Republicans expected to hold fewer than 185 House seats, down from 219 now, and that of eight key Senate races five lean Democratic in Alaska, Kansas, Maine, Ohio and Texas, two lean Republican in Nebraska and South Carolina, and Iowa remains a toss-up. items.title: Tonight: Seven Hours of Poll Closings, Then the Waiting
items.body:
Tonight: Seven Hours of Poll Closings, Then the Waiting

Election night, for the prediction markets, starts at 6 PM ET and does not end at midnight. The first polls close in the Eastern-time parts of Indiana and Kentucky at 6 PM, and the last, in Alaska's western Aleutians, close at 1 AM ET on Wednesday (Kalshi News). Between those two moments, roughly $1.9 billion of midterm positions will be repriced state by state, and the two big venues have built the night into their products: Kalshi's new Election Day field visualization positions each race as a circle placed by the favored candidate's price and sized by volume, with accuracy scores and low-volume warnings attached (NextPredict), while Polymarket's 2026 Midterms Hub pairs live results with live prices on the same screen.

The hour-by-hour shape is known in advance. At 7 PM ET, Georgia, South Carolina, Vermont and Virginia close, along with most of Florida: the South Carolina Senate market, priced at an identical 73 cents for Graham on both venues, gets its first real test. At 7:30 PM, North Carolina, Ohio and West Virginia close; Ohio's Senate special election has Sherrod Brown at 71 cents on both Polymarket and Kalshi (Vegas Insider). The 8 PM wave is the biggest of the night: Pennsylvania, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey and most of Michigan and Texas, including Pennsylvania's 1st district, the board's biggest overnight mover. Arkansas follows at 8:30. At 9 PM, New York, Arizona, Colorado, Iowa, Minnesota, Wisconsin and the last of Texas and Michigan close: Iowa's Senate race, the tightest big race on the board at 52 percent for Hinson (Covers), and Kansas, where the Senate market flipped to a record 63 percent for Hamilton this week (NextPredict), report in that window. Montana, Nevada and Utah close at 10 PM; California, Washington and Oregon at 11 PM; Hawaii and most of Alaska at midnight.

Television is part of the market structure tonight. CBS News will incorporate Kalshi data into its Election 2026 coverage from 5 PM ET, while CNN and Fox News will not feature odds (NextPredict), and the venues have struck media deals across CNN, CBS, CNBC and Dow Jones ahead of the midterms (Phemex News). The rooms are set too: Kalshi is hosting election-night watch parties in New York, Washington, Chicago, Austin and Los Angeles, and Polymarket figures join the All-In podcast's 7 PM ET livestream.

The part of tonight that decides money is not the closing times. It is the settlement rules, and the two venues wrote different ones. Kalshi's House and Senate control markets can settle early on a consensus of media calls; if the calls never align, the fallback is formal, the party of the Speaker for the House and the party of the president pro tempore for the Senate on February 1, 2027 (PredictionTape; PredictReport). Polymarket's single-race markets resolve when the Associated Press, Fox News and NBC have all called the race for the same candidate, and otherwise wait for the official certified result. A race can trade at 95 cents for days before it pays.

That gap between priced and paid is where tonight's risk sits. Close races trigger recounts, and a race in recount will not settle on a media call; its market can stay open for weeks. A runoff, Georgia being the standing example, pushes a Senate seat past election night entirely, and if chamber control runs through that seat, both platforms wait with it. California counts mail ballots that arrive up to a week after Election Day, so its district markets can stay live and moving long after the state's 11 PM close. And the thin end of the board will move first and fastest: district markets trade far less than the control markets, a single large order can move them several points (Vantage Predictions), and the Anti-Corruption Data Collective found 96 percent of congressional markets could be shifted five cents for $3,500 or less.

So the watch list writes itself. Watch the 8 PM wave for whether the Senate price, 78 percent as polls opened, survives Pennsylvania and Michigan. Watch the thin districts for moves that are one order deep. Watch whether Kalshi's media-consensus trigger and Polymarket's three-network rule produce the same winners at the same speed. The prices will call the night long before the contracts pay for it, and the distance between those two moments is the real story of Election Night 2026.

Sources: Kalshi News, NextPredict, Vegas Insider, Covers, Phemex News, PredictionTape, PredictReport, Vantage Predictions, Action Network

items.title: Follow the Money: Kalshi's $1.7 Billion Election
items.body:
Follow the Money: Kalshi's $1.7 Billion Election

Follow the money in the 2026 midterms and most of it leads to one venue. DeFi Rate's Election Day tally put total midterm trading at $1.94 billion, with Kalshi accounting for $1.70 billion of it. The same tally's early-morning split showed the rest of the field: Polymarket at $78 million, Polymarket US at $34 million and DraftKings Predictions at $68 million. An earlier snapshot from Trefis told the same story at an earlier hour: Kalshi at about $1.1 billion against about $340 million for Polymarket, roughly 3.2 times the volume. Kalshi reported $1.33 billion across all midterm bets as of Monday (Reuters), and its share of the combined two-venue volume has been the structural story of the cycle: Polymarket's combined market share fell to 17.2 percent in the 30 days before October 29 as Kalshi pulled away (Gaming America).

Where the money sits matters as much as how much there is. The two biggest single markets are the chamber markets: House control above $219 million in volume and Senate control above $153 million (Action Network). Kalshi's Congress balance-of-power market has passed $106 million on its own. The Anti-Corruption Data Collective counts $431 million wagered on congressional markets this cycle, nearly triple 2024 (RG.org), spread across more than 28,000 midterm markets. Politics is not a category on these venues today, it is the venue: DeFi Rate's top-50 board shows politics taking $44 million of $51 million in 24-hour volume, and its category trackers showed politics payouts of $211 million in 24 hours, up 94 percent (DeFi Rate).

The contract counts underline the dollar gap. Kalshi traded 286 million midterm contracts by Election Eve, 28 million of them in the last 24 hours, with 195 million still open. In October, the last full month before the vote, Kalshi logged about $65 billion in volume against about $10 billion for Polymarket US (CryptoBriefing). Even the map markets carry size now: the Senate swing-state map traded $5.6 million in 24 hours, 3.8 times its daily average. Money also moved around the markets, not just through them: the two venues gave at least $5 million to political organizations this cycle, and Polymarket paid creators at least $350,000 (So Does It Matter).

The flow underneath the totals has a shape. Polymarket whale flow totaled $8.9 million across 418 large trades in 24 hours (Rivo). At the top of the trader boards, one wallet, googleplayB, leads Polymarket with $3.0 million in profit on $23.1 million traded, the weekly leaderboard tops out at $3.95 million in profit for the leading wallet (PolyTrackers), and Kalshi's daily board was led by EdZachary with $217,300 in profit (Rivo). Concentration shows up in the politics book too: a single Polymarket wallet holds $145,000 of the $229,000 that the platform's top traders have backing Democratic Senate control (Action Network). When the Senate market moves tonight, a meaningful share of the other side of the trade is a handful of wallets.

Some of the money is buying information the slow way. Kalshi and Polymarket traders have been canvassing voters in person to find a midterm information edge (PANews), knocking on doors to build the ground read that the order book cannot see. It is the logical end of a market that pays for being right early: if prices aggregate public information instantly, the remaining edge is information that is not public yet, gathered one doorstep at a time.

The business underneath the betting is scaling with it. Polymarket traders paid about $118.9 million in fees in the 30 days to November 3 (Dexsheet), and the venues came into Election Day fresh off a record October: $123.3 billion in total prediction-market volume, with Kalshi accounting for about 80 percent (TokenPost). Kalshi also raised $1 billion at a $40 billion valuation in the run-up to the vote, a single-source report the market has not independently confirmed (TokenPost).

The concentration cuts both ways, and tonight will show it. A Senate market carried by a few large wallets can reprice violently when results start landing in the close states, and a venue holding $1.70 billion of the $1.94 billion total will set the reference price every other board follows. The money has already voted on who runs this market. After tonight, it finds out what its votes were worth.

Sources: DeFi Rate, Reuters, Trefis, Gaming America, Action Network, RG.org, Rivo, PolyTrackers, PANews, Dexsheet, TokenPost

items.title: Where the Money Disagrees: Markets, Polls and Models on Election Day
items.body:
Where the Money Disagrees: Markets, Polls and Models on Election Day

The most informative prices on Election Day are not the ones that agree with the polls. They are the ones that do not, and this morning the board has a clear set of them, starting at the top: Senate control. Action Network's Election Day comparison put Democratic Senate control at 70 percent on Kalshi and 73 percent on Polymarket, against forecasting models sitting in the high 70s. The market is paying for the Senate, but it is charging a discount to the models to do it. Aggregated prices told the same story a day earlier: BetInt's market aggregate on Monday implied 95 percent for the House and 76 percent for the Senate (Reuters), and by the time polls opened the Senate price had climbed to 78 percent (InvestingLive). The gap between market and model has narrowed all morning without closing.

Some of that discount is scar tissue. Reuters' Morning Bid noted traders are wary after the Brazil miss, when heavily traded markets got a major election wrong. Set against that, academic work keeps finding the markets well calibrated at scale: a 2025 Vanderbilt study of nearly 2,500 markets on the 2024 election is among the research Reuters cited this morning. Tonight is a live rematch between those two findings, with more than $1.48 billion riding on the outcome.

District markets show the divergence in miniature. Vantage Predictions' Election Day snapshot, comparing this morning with Monday afternoon, ranked Pennsylvania's 1st district as the biggest overnight move on the House board: Democrat Harvie rose from 55 percent to 64.5 percent against Republican incumbent Brian Fitzpatrick, on the average of Kalshi and Polymarket prices, while Colorado's 3rd moved the other way, with Republican Jeff Hurd slipping from 62.5 percent to 55.8 percent. These are thin markets, and Vantage itself cautions that a single large order can move them several points. A nine-and-a-half-point overnight move is either information arriving or one trader's conviction, and the price alone cannot tell you which.

South Carolina's Senate race is the opposite case: the two venues agree with each other exactly and disagree with the polling. Graham is priced at 73 cents on both Polymarket and Kalshi, with Andrews at 28 cents on both, an exact cross-venue match, while recent polls run from a one-point Graham edge to a 48-48 tie in the New York Times/Siena survey (Action Network). A tied poll and a 73-cent price can both be honest: the market is pricing incumbency, fundraising and the state's lean on top of the survey snapshot. If the surveys are right and the race is truly even, 73 cents is the most expensive favorite on tonight's board. If the market is right, the polls missed the state's shape.

Alaska offers a third kind of gap, model against market. Sikt's AI forecast puts Mary Peltola at 53 percent against a market average of 72 percent (Sikt Intelligence). One of them is wrong by nearly twenty points, and tonight will grade both. Kansas, meanwhile, produced the week's biggest repricing: Democrat Adam Hamilton climbed to a record 63 percent on Kalshi in the Senate race, up 23 points in a week (NextPredict), a move large enough that either the race genuinely broke open or the market spent a week catching up to itself. Florida's governor race moved the other way, with Byron Donalds sliding 15 points in a week to 64 percent on Kalshi (DeFi Rate).

For all the disagreement at the edges, the venues rarely disagree with each other. Across 54 matched outcomes, Kalshi and Polymarket prices average a 1.2-point gap (PolymarketTrader). The real argument is not venue against venue. It is the combined market against the polls and models, and it is concentrated exactly where the money is thinnest: the Anti-Corruption Data Collective found 96 percent of congressional markets could be shifted five cents for $3,500 or less (Gambling Insider). Deep control markets are hard to move and have earned their calibration record. Thin district markets are easy to move and have not. Election night will test both kinds at once, and the honest read of today's divergences is that they live almost entirely in the second kind.

Sources: Action Network, Reuters, InvestingLive, Vantage Predictions, Sikt Intelligence, NextPredict, DeFi Rate, PolymarketTrader, Gambling Insider

items.title: Election Day's Whole Board: $1.9 Billion Riding on Two Chambers
items.body:
Election Day's Whole Board: $1.9 Billion Riding on Two Chambers

By the time the first polls opened this morning, tracked midterm trading across the prediction-market venues had reached $1.93 billion, and the day's running total kept climbing: DeFi Rate's Election Day tally put the figure at $1.79 billion early this morning and $1.94 billion soon after, with Kalshi alone accounting for $1.70 billion of it. Reuters, in its Election Day assessment, counted more than $1.48 billion wagered on the midterms and called tonight the biggest forecasting test the industry has faced.

The board itself tells a consistent story at the top. Democrats are priced at 93 cents on Kalshi and 94 cents on Polymarket to win the House, and as polls opened this morning the price had firmed to between 94 and 95 percent (Sikt Intelligence; InvestingLive). The Senate is the live question: priced at 74 percent on Kalshi and 76 percent on Polymarket in the earliest reads, it moved through 75.9 percent on Election Day morning to 78 percent as polls opened (Vantage Predictions; InvestingLive). The Democratic sweep of both chambers is priced at 78 percent on Polymarket and 74 percent on Kalshi (KuCoin), and Kalshi's own Congress balance-of-power market has passed $106 million in volume with the sweep at 75 percent there.

The single biggest markets are the control markets themselves. Action Network's midterm guide puts the House control market above $219 million in volume and the Senate control market above $153 million. The Anti-Corruption Data Collective counts $431 million wagered on congressional markets in the 2026 cycle, nearly triple the 2024 figure (RG.org). Kalshi reported $1.33 billion in trading volume across all midterm bets as of Monday, against roughly $145 million on Polymarket's congressional markets, according to ACDC figures cited by Reuters. More than 28,000 midterm markets have been opened.

Contract counts show the same scale. Kalshi's midterm markets passed 371 million contracts traded, with Democrats at 75 percent for the Senate and 93 percent for the House on that read (PredictionMarketPicks). On Election Eve alone, Kalshi traded 286 million contracts across its Senate, House and chamber-control markets, with 195 million contracts still open. Politics dominates the cross-venue board: DeFi Rate's top-50 split shows politics taking $44 million of $51 million in 24-hour volume across 37 of the top 50 markets.

Below the control markets, the race board is deep but uneven. Kalshi lists 13 midterm toss-up races with neither candidate above 60 percent, including Iowa's Senate race, where Ashley Hinson is priced at 52 percent in the tightest big race on the board (Covers). Governor races carry real volume too: Ohio Democrat Amy Acton is priced at 82 percent and Georgia Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms at 71 percent (Action Network), while California's governor race sits at 98 cents for Xavier Becerra on Polymarket (Action Network).

The day did not start from zero. Monday's closing aggregates, compiled by BetInt from market prices, implied a 95 percent chance of Democrats taking the House and 76 percent for the Senate (Reuters), and Kalshi's Election Eve numbers set the scale: 286 million contracts traded across its Senate, House and chamber-control markets, 28 million of them in the final 24 hours, with 195 million contracts still open and traders putting $30 million into election markets in a single day. The November catalog shows how wide the board has become: Polymarket lists 14,363 active markets for November, and its dated calendar runs to 1,610 markets, led by 1,210 election markets (Polymarket; PolymarketTrader).

The legal backdrop follows the money into Election Day. Wisconsin is the only state warning voters they could face prosecution for trading on an election they vote in, and a Competitive Enterprise Institute suit seeks to shield those voters (Deadspin). Senators Warren and Curtis have pressed both venues on election insider-trading controls, with answers due today (Financial Regulation News). And a new bill would ban candidates from betting on their own elections, with penalties of at least $10,000 (Crypto News), after several candidates were suspended this cycle for exactly that.

What the whole board says, hours before the first results: the House is close to settled in price, the Senate is a genuinely open market that has firmed toward Democrats all morning, and the sweep trades at roughly three-in-four. The $1.9 billion now has to survive contact with actual votes.

Sources: DeFi Rate, Vantage Predictions, InvestingLive, Sikt Intelligence, KuCoin, Reuters, Action Network, PredictionMarketPicks, Covers, Deadspin, Financial Regulation News, Crypto News

items.title: Australia's ASIC says a retail prediction market is unlikely to pass its public interest test for a market licence
items.body: - **Australia's ASIC says a retail prediction market is unlikely to pass its public interest test for a market licence** — The Australian Securities and Investments Commission said on October 30 that it is not currently convinced prediction markets for retail clients are in the public interest, with Chair Sarah Court noting the contracts share their all-or-nothing structure with binary options, which ASIC has banned for retail clients until October 2031. items.title: The Favorite Vanished: Game of the Year Flipped in Three Weeks
items.body:
The Favorite Vanished: Game of the Year Flipped in Three Weeks

When Polymarket opened its Golden Joystick Awards Ultimate Game of the Year market on October 13, the race looked settled. Saros led the 18-game field at 78 percent, with 007: First Light next at 50 percent, in a multi-outcome book where rival prices can overlap. Three weeks later, neither number survived.

Read on November 2, the market has a new leader and a new shape. Resident Evil Requiem now fronts the field at 52 percent, priced at 52 cents a share, and 007: First Light has fallen to second at 19 percent. Saros, the 78 percent opening favorite, no longer sits in the top two at all. The market has traded $34.1K in total since launch and is scheduled to resolve on or around November 30, when the award is announced.

The flip is also a lesson in thin books. A $34.1K lifetime total is small next to the election and crypto boards, so a handful of committed buyers can rewrite a culture market in days. The wider awards board is busier: Polymarket lists 105 live awards markets, with $141.7K traded across them in the last 24 hours, as traders price everything from Oscar nominations to season MVP races months before any envelope is opened.

That is the quiet appeal of culture markets. They turn fan consensus into a price long before critics, polls or award panels speak, and they update the moment sentiment moves. This one says the Game of the Year race was never settled at all. It just looked that way at 78 percent.

Sources: Polymarket, PolymarketTrader

items.title: 22.5 Percent on Both Books: The Spurs Price Nobody Disputes
items.body:
22.5 Percent on Both Books: The Spurs Price Nobody Disputes

Two rival exchanges, two separate order books, one identical number. On November 2, San Antonio trades at 22.5 percent to win the 2027 NBA championship on Polymarket and at 22.5 percent on Kalshi. On the biggest futures market in basketball, the rivals do not disagree at all.

The agreement runs through the board. Across 54 outcomes priced on both exchanges, the average gap is just 1.1 percentage points. Oklahoma City is the widest NBA split, at 12.5 percent on Polymarket against 14.5 percent on Kalshi, and Boston shows the same two-point spread in reverse, 7.5 percent against 5.5 percent. Philadelphia sits at 11.6 and 12.5 percent, Houston at 7.6 and 6.5 percent.

Tonight shows the same discipline in miniature. All 15 NBA games are priced on both venues, and the widest gaps on the whole slate are a single point. San Antonio is the night's biggest favorite at 91 percent against Utah, the first tip is at 7:00 PM ET, the last at 10:00 PM ET, the closest game prices the Lakers at 55 percent, and the highest total is 239.5 points, with $105,220 traded on the most active game.

Football echoes it. Seattle prices at 8.5 percent to win the pro football championship on both exchanges, and tonight's Chicago at Seattle Monday night game has already traded about $1.86 million on Kalshi before kickoff.

When two competing markets land on the same price to the decimal, that price stops looking like one venue's opinion. It starts looking like the number.

items.title: The Machines Are the Market Now: AI Agents Take Their Seats on the Book
items.body:
The Machines Are the Market Now: AI Agents Take Their Seats on the Book

Look at who actually makes money on the biggest prediction market and a pattern jumps out: fourteen of the twenty most profitable wallets on Polymarket are bots, according to FXVerify's reporting. One wallet turned roughly $300 into more than $400,000 in a single month by trading fifteen-minute Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana contracts, exploiting the small lag between prices on the big crypto exchanges and prices on the prediction market. A 2025 study of a full year of Polymarket trading estimated arbitrage strategies extracted about $40 million from the platform. The fastest money in forecasting is no longer forecasting at all. It is plumbing.

That division of labor is becoming the market's structure. Machines excel at the mechanical edges: scanning order books for mispriced pairs, arbitraging the same event across venues, quoting both sides of thin markets and tightening spreads for everyone else. The infrastructure now assumes non-human customers. Polymarket's data and trading APIs are built for programmatic access, model-context-protocol servers stream live order books directly into AI agent frameworks, venues market themselves to autonomous agents, and purpose-built agents trade around the clock without sleep, fear or a favorite team.

But give the machines the actual forecasting job and the record humbles quickly. In the Prediction Arena experiment, six frontier AI models traded autonomously on Kalshi for 57 days and every one of them lost money, down between 16% and 31%. More research did not rescue them; the study found the volume of a model's research had little correlation with its returns. Meanwhile the profit distribution stays brutally concentrated: a Wall Street Journal analysis found about 67% of Polymarket's profit accrues to the top 0.1% of accounts, a leaderboard dominated by speed, size and systems rather than opinions.

The synthesis is the story. Prediction markets are becoming machine-readable probability infrastructure, a layer where prices are quoted in an API, consumed by software, and increasingly set by software too. That makes markets faster, tighter and harder to fool with stale prices. It does not make them oracles. The bots earn by correcting the price; the price still needs humans, with information and conviction, to be worth correcting toward.

For everyone else, the practical lesson is the same one Article One of this series delivered from the other side: know which game you are playing. Against a latency bot, a human clicking a price is the exit liquidity. In a slow, information-driven market, the machine is just another counterparty. The book now seats both species, and the edge belongs to whoever knows which seat they are in.

Sources: FXVerify; Prediction Arena study; Wall Street Journal

items.title: 286 Million Contracts: Election Eve Is Now a Trading Day
items.body:
286 Million Contracts: Election Eve Is Now a Trading Day

One day before the November 3 vote, Kalshi alone has traded 286,241,295 contracts across its Senate, House and chamber-control markets. Another 28,054,712 contracts changed hands in the last 24 hours, and 195,407,038 contracts are still open across 100 live races, 285 tradeable contracts, 35 Senate races and 66 competitive House districts.

The money is not spread thin. Traders put $30 million into election markets in the past 24 hours, and politics took 35 of the top 50 markets on the combined board, worth $27 million of its $33 million in 24-hour volume. The single biggest market is the Senate swing-state map: $5.6 million in 24 hours across 128 outcomes, trading at 3.8 times its daily average, with None leading at 32 cents.

The chamber picture is priced, not polled. Democrats are at 72 percent to win the Senate and 94 percent to win the House, and a Democratic sweep trades at 71 cents on Kalshi on $2.0 million in 24 hours. The balance-of-power contract itself has traded 61.0 million contracts, with 48.9 million still open.

The tightest race shows where the doubt remains. In Iowa, Ashley Hinson leads at 53 cents in the highest-volume Senate race the market still cannot call, with 9.7 million contracts traded and 5.5 million open. In Maine, the race for the 51st seat prices Troy Jackson at 73 percent.

Election Eve used to be a night for final polls. Now it has an order book, open interest, and a closing rush that starts before the first precinct opens.

Sources: PredictionMarketsPicks, DeFi Rate

Won the Trade, Met the Tax Man: The Unsettled Tax Life of a Prediction-Market Dollar

Every winning trade creates two events: the settlement, and the tax question. In the United States, prediction-market profits are taxable income whether or not any platform sends you a form, and that is where the certainty ends. As of 2026, the IRS has issued no specific guidance on event contracts, which leaves traders and their accountants arguing about a deceptively simple question: what, exactly, is a prediction-market dollar?

Three answers circulate in professional practice. The conservative one treats net profits as ordinary income, taxed at marginal rates from 10% to 37%, with net losses simply not deductible. The common middle position reports gains as capital gains. The most favorable, and the most contested, is Section 1256: contracts traded on a CFTC-regulated designated contract market are argued to qualify for the futures-style 60/40 blend, 60% long-term and 40% short-term regardless of holding period. One worked example puts a 32%-bracket trader with $50,000 of gains at roughly $10,900 of federal tax under Section 1256 against about $16,000 at ordinary rates. The catch is qualification: the IRS has historically read Section 1256 narrowly, and no ruling blesses event contracts by name.

The fourth possibility is the one traders least want to hear: gambling treatment. Under it, winnings are ordinary income and losses are deductible only by itemizers, and only against winnings. Worse, starting with the 2026 tax year, a new federal cap limits gambling-loss deductions to 90% of losses, which can leave a break-even bettor owing tax on income they never kept. Whether sports event contracts fall on the gambling side of the line is precisely the kind of question the missing IRS guidance would answer.

Reporting adds its own friction. Tax guides disagree about what platforms send: Kalshi provides profit-and-loss statements and may issue forms for interest and rewards, while several guides report that neither Kalshi nor Polymarket issues a 1099 covering trading gains, leaving the reporting burden on the trader either way. Crypto-settled platforms add a second ledger, because moving stablecoins in and out can itself create records to reconcile. State treatment varies too; some states follow the federal approach and others do not.

The practical discipline is boring and decisive: keep every trade record, reconcile it against whatever the platform reports, and decide the characterization question with a professional before filing, not after a notice arrives. This article is general information about a genuinely unsettled area, not tax advice. The market prices uncertainty for a living. On taxes, for now, traders have to hold it themselves.

Answers Due on Election Day: Two Senators Put the Exchanges on Record

On October 28, Senators Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts and John Curtis of Utah wrote to Kalshi chief executive Tarek Mansour and Polymarket chief executive Shayne Coplan demanding answers by November 3, Election Day, on how each exchange stops insider trading and manipulation in its midterm contracts.

The letter, published October 29, asks four things: what safeguards are in place now, what each exchange does beyond screening Federal Election Commission filings to stop campaigns and others with material nonpublic information from trading, which cases it has referred to the CFTC, and how it detects manipulation.

It leans on three episodes: candidates who traded contracts on their own races in 2025 and April 2026, alleged manipulation on Polymarket's 2024 presidential market put at roughly one third of that market's volume, and an NPR investigation into campaign insiders who traded ahead of internal polling, with at least one trade verified against market records.

The timing is the scale. More than $1.4 billion has traded on the 2026 midterms, nearly $1.1 billion of it on Kalshi and more than $340 million on Polymarket, and Kalshi has already suspended six 2026 candidates for betting on their own races. Kalshi says it prohibits insider trading, blocks candidates and campaign staff using FEC payroll data, and has set up an independent market integrity committee.

The letter has no legal force and suspends no market. What it does is put both exchanges on record, in writing, on the day voters decide the Senate and House races their contracts price. Whether either reply is published, and whether the CFTC acts, is now the story after the polls close.

Sources: Senate Banking Committee, The Hill, CNN, The Daily Upside

items.title: The Watchers: How Prediction Markets Learned to Police Themselves
items.body:
The Watchers: How Prediction Markets Learned to Police Themselves

A prediction market is only worth its price if the game is not rigged. That sounds obvious, but it is the industry's hardest engineering problem: markets on elections, wars, rate decisions and ballgames create enormous incentives for anyone holding non-public information to trade on it first. The events of 2026 have forced the industry to build, in public and under pressure, the integrity stack that mature financial markets spent decades assembling.

The threat is not hypothetical. In April 2026, an active-duty U.S. Army soldier was charged with using confidential information to bet on Polymarket ahead of the capture of Venezuela's Nicolás Maduro. A former White House teleprompter operator agreed to pay more than $172,000 to settle charges that he traded on Kalshi using advance access to presidential speeches. Both cases carried the same lesson: the information edge in event markets is real, it is valuable, and someone will try to monetize it.

The regulated end of the industry starts with identity and surveillance. Kalshi operates as a CFTC Designated Contract Market, the same regulatory category as the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, with mandatory know-your-customer checks, position reporting, anti-manipulation rules and individual exposure capped at $7 million. It runs market surveillance with IC360 to flag suspicious activity and identify people prohibited from trading, and both Kalshi and Polymarket now require employment verification for traders in sensitive markets, so a locker-room or situation-room connection is harder to hide.

The newest layer is cooperation with the people who own the information. On October 26, 2026, the NBA signed an information-sharing memorandum of understanding with the CFTC, the third major U.S. league after Major League Baseball and the NHL to do so, aimed at insider trading and fraud. The league named Kalshi and Polymarket its preferred prediction market exchanges on terms that prohibit league and team personnel from trading NBA contracts, restrict which markets may be listed, require cooperation on suspicious-trading investigations, and settle authorized markets on official league data distributed by Sportradar, an authoritative record instead of a judgment call.

None of this makes manipulation impossible, and the standard is still being contested: the NFL has declined to partner and instead pressed for tougher integrity rules. But the architecture is now visible. Identity at the door, surveillance on the tape, settlement on official data, and a direct line between the league, the exchange and the regulator. Prediction markets asked to be treated like financial markets. Policing themselves like financial markets is the price of that ambition.

Sources: Cointelegraph; FinanceFeeds; The Block; BS Capital Markets

items.title: College Basketball Is Back, and the Exchanges Cannot Agree
items.body:
College Basketball Is Back, and the Exchanges Cannot Agree

College basketball's 2026-27 season opens today, November 2, in Rock Hill, South Carolina, and the prediction markets are already arguing with each other. At the Field of 68 Showcase, High Point is a clear favorite over Liberty on both exchanges, at 78 percent on Polymarket and 77 cents on Kalshi, but almost every other line on the board splits the two venues.

The widest split is the spread. High Point minus 7.5 trades at 54 percent on Polymarket, right in line with the sportsbook consensus, but at 69 cents on Kalshi, where the Yes and No prices add up to 122 cents, the tell of a thin opening-day book that has not yet been arbitraged tight. The total agrees better: over 154.5 sits at 55 percent on Polymarket and 54 cents on Kalshi.

In the morning game at the same arena, the exchanges cannot even pick the same favorite. Winthrop against Queens is a coin flip with a twist: Polymarket leans Winthrop, 60 percent to 59, while Kalshi leans Queens, 59 cents to 58. Sportsbooks make Queens a 2-point favorite with a total of 165.5, a third opinion that neither board fully matches.

The caution is understandable. High Point returns from a 31-5 season that included an NCAA Tournament upset of Wisconsin, while Liberty, the defending Conference USA regular-season champion, leads the all-time series 24-17. With every team at 0-0 and no current-season data, opening-day prices are built on last year's tape, and the gaps between venues are where that uncertainty shows.

Those gaps will not survive tip-off for long. Season openers are the thinnest books of the year, and the first live trading usually pulls the exchanges into line within minutes. For one morning, college basketball has two prices for the same game, and both are trading.
