items.title: First Team In: Kalshi Signs the 76ers
items.body:
First Team In: Kalshi Signs the 76ers

The Philadelphia 76ers became the first NBA team to name an official prediction market partner on Friday, signing a multiyear agreement with Kalshi. The deal puts Kalshi in the arena, in the 76ers mobile app and on the team's ticketing platform — the first time an NBA franchise has sold that space to an exchange.

The timing is the story. The team deal lands just four days after the NBA itself named Kalshi and Polymarket its Preferred Prediction Market Exchanges on October 26, with DraftKings expanded as an authorized operator. The league framework gives both exchanges official NBA data via Sportradar, NBA intellectual property and marketing rights, in exchange for integrity rules that prohibit league and team personnel from trading NBA contracts.

The money around the players is moving just as fast. LeBron James signed a reported $15 million annual endorsement agreement with Polymarket in September, Giannis Antetokounmpo became a Kalshi shareholder earlier this year, and Kevin Durant and Devin Booker have established their own ties to operators.

The trading underneath it all is enormous: prediction markets generated more than $14 billion in notional volume over the October 24-25 weekend alone, including more than $10 billion on Kalshi, according to Aldrin Research, and sports account for roughly 80 percent of all prediction market volume. The NFL remains the last major league holding out — and has backed state regulators at the Supreme Court, where a ruling could come as early as 2027.

items.title: Seventy Percent Says the Fed Hikes in December
items.body:
Seventy Percent Says the Fed Hikes in December

The Federal Reserve held rates at 3.75% to 4.00% on October 28, but it was not a quiet hold. The vote was 10-2, with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack both voting for a quarter-point hike right away. Prediction markets read the dissents as a forwarding address: the hike the committee skipped in October is now priced to arrive in December.

As of October 30 at 5:00 PM ET, Kalshi prices a 25-point hike on December 9 at 69%, a hold at 28%, a 50-point hike at about 3% and a cut at 1% — a 72% chance of a hike in total. Polymarket prices the same 25-point hike at 70.5%, and fed funds futures are higher still at 73.3%. DeFi Rate's last trades tell the same story: Kalshi at 68.5 cents with $60K traded in 24 hours, Polymarket at 70.5 cents with $173K traded.

The crowd has earned some trust here. The market favorite has won 15 of 15 Fed decisions since 2025 on Kalshi and Polymarket, and October was graded close: Polymarket closed the hold at 95.5% and Kalshi at 94.5%. December's hike odds first closed above 50% on August 15 and sit at 73% on the latest daily close, even after slipping 3 points this week from 72% to 69% on Kalshi's decision contract.

Beyond December, the path goes quiet. January 27 prices a hike at just 26% to 28% against a 71% hold, and March is a coin flip at 50% hike, 47% hold. Kalshi's dot-plot ladder, which prices the Fed's own year-end 2026 projection, implies a median dot of 4.00% to 4.10% — exactly one more hike, delivered in December and then a pause.

What moves it next is data, starting with payrolls on November 6. The statement lands at 2:00 PM ET on December 9 with a new dot plot attached. Until then, every inflation print is a trade: hot, and 70% becomes 80%; soft, and the two dissenters start to look early rather than right.

items.title: Five Minutes at a Time
items.body:
Five Minutes at a Time

Prediction markets used to ask where Bitcoin would close the month. Now they ask where it closes in the next five minutes.

On October 28, Polymarket's regulated U.S. platform launched five-minute up-or-down contracts on Bitcoin, Ether, Solana and XRP. Each contract asks one question: does the price finish the five-minute window above or below where it started? A correct call pays $1 a share; a wrong one pays nothing. With 288 windows a day per asset, the platform now runs crypto contracts at five-minute, 15-minute, hourly, daily, weekly and monthly intervals.

The format is proven. Polymarket's international platform introduced five-minute crypto contracts in February and generated roughly $4 billion in volume in their first six months. The U.S. versions run through QCX LLC under CFTC oversight and settle against CF Benchmarks pricing using time-weighted averages, a safeguard added in August.

The launch lands under a microscope: the CFTC is reviewing Polymarket's compliance with its 2022 settlement even as the contracts go live. Speed is the product now, and the scrutiny scales with it.

items.title: The World Series Became a Trading Floor
items.body:
The World Series Became a Trading Floor

The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays on October 28 to win the 2026 World Series. On Kalshi, the series was also one of the biggest trading events of the year.

World Series games drew more than $180 million in volume on the exchange: $39.7 million on Game 1, $35.1 million on Game 2, $20.2 million on Game 3, a series-high $51.4 million on the extra-innings Game 4, and $37.9 million on the Game 5 clincher. Nearly 28 million contracts changed hands on the World Series winner market alone, and Kalshi says baseball volume is up more than 36-fold year over year, with nearly $60 million traded on World Series futures before the first pitch.

The pattern is the story: volume spiked when games were close and sagged in the 10-1 blowout. Traders were not betting on baseball so much as trading its uncertainty, pitch by pitch.

The 2027 market opened immediately. The Dodgers lead at 22.7%, the champion Brewers sit second at 11.9%, and the Yankees are third at 11%.

items.title: Coinbase's $200 Million Side Door
items.body:
Coinbase's $200 Million Side Door

Coinbase's fastest-growing product is not crypto trading. It is prediction markets.

Reporting third-quarter results on October 29, Coinbase said its prediction markets business passed $200 million in annualized revenue, up from more than $100 million in the second quarter. Revenue from the product has compounded at 82% per quarter since launch, daily traders rose more than 60% in the quarter, and CEO Brian Armstrong called it one of the fastest-growing products by revenue in Coinbase history.

The detail that matters: more than half the contracts traded in Q3 were non-sports. Prediction markets are pulling in users who then trade crypto — Coinbase says prediction traders drive incremental spot volume — and the revenue is, in CFO Alesia Haas's words, less correlated to crypto volatility.

Next comes vertical integration. The CFTC cleared Coinbase Clearing LLC as a derivatives clearing organization on September 28, and Armstrong told investors Coinbase can now list its own prediction contracts instead of only routing flow to partners. In a slow crypto quarter, the side door is becoming a main entrance.

Gold has been money for five thousand years. As of this week, it is also a 15-minute prediction market.

Polymarket has launched 15-minute up-or-down contracts on gold and silver, settled by Chainlink price streams, extending the high-speed format beyond crypto for the first time. Chainlink is now the platform's official oracle for up/down markets, and the infrastructure has already carried more than $11 billion of volume across Polymarket's five- and 15-minute crypto markets. Equities and foreign exchange are next in line.

The timing is not an accident. Gold just fell below $3,900 to a fresh 2026 low ahead of the midterms, and Kalshi's own commodities business passed $100 million in annualized trading fees within three months of launch. On Kalshi's 15-minute boards, gold alone now trades tens of millions of contracts a day.

The oldest store of value in the world now resolves like a crypto candle — a quarter-hour at a time.

items.body:
Google Now Answers Election Questions With a Market

Ask Google for an election forecast this fall, and there is a coin flip's chance the answer comes from a betting market.

A CasinoReviews.net study of 140 Google results pages across 14 U.S. cities found Polymarket or Kalshi on page one for half of everyday forecast searches like 'election forecast' and 'midterm polls.' Kalshi appeared on all 28 pages sampled for 'senate odds' and 'midterm odds.' Almost nobody is searching for odds — about 1 in 120 midterm searches uses betting language — yet for half of the rest, Google surfaces a market anyway.

The sharpest finding: the platforms appeared in all eight cities tested in states where election betting is banned. Twenty-four states prohibit it outright, while federally regulated exchanges offer election contracts nationwide — a conflict now being argued in court.

The polls are no longer the forecast of record. The market is — whether the searcher asked for it or not.

items.title: The $65 Billion Month
items.body:
The $65 Billion Month

October was the biggest month prediction markets have ever had — and it was not close.

Kalshi traded approximately $65 billion in October, 10% above its September record. Polymarket US reached $10 billion, up roughly 15% on its previous high. Open interest set records on both platforms: $2.05 billion on Kalshi and $384 million on Polymarket US. A year ago, Kalshi's entire October was about $4.4 billion.

The structure of the market flipped with the scale. Kalshi now accounts for nearly 83% of combined volume across itself and both Polymarket platforms, and U.S.-regulated venues hold 95.6% of the total. The offshore upstart era is over; the volume lives on regulated American exchanges now.

The test comes next week. The midterms end Tuesday, and post-election volume will show whether October was a peak or a plateau — whether $65 billion months are the new baseline or an election-season spike.

items.title: Fifteen Percent Is the Favorite: The Super Bowl Market Has No Front-Runner
items.body:
Fifteen Percent Is the Favorite: The Super Bowl Market Has No Front-Runner

Super Bowl LXI is on February 14, 2027 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, and the prediction markets cannot find a favorite. The San Francisco 49ers lead the board at about 15% on DeFi Rate's cross-exchange average — 15.5 cents on Kalshi, 14.1 cents on Polymarket. A 15% favorite means the market thinks someone else wins about 85% of the time.

The chase pack is tight. The Buffalo Bills sit second at 12% — 11.5 cents on Kalshi, 12 cents on Polymarket — and the Kansas City Chiefs are third at 9.7%, priced higher on Polymarket (10.1 cents) than on Kalshi (9.5 cents). The Seattle Seahawks and Chicago Bears are next at about 7.5% each, with the Los Angeles Rams at 6.5%.

The week's movers show how unsettled it is. Seattle climbed from 6% to 8% on Kalshi's daily close and Cincinnati from 4% to 6%, the two biggest gains of the last seven days. Houston fell from 4% to 2%. At the top, San Francisco slipped 1 point on the week while Buffalo gained 1 point — first and second are converging, not separating.

The money is deep even without a leader. On Kalshi alone, the Rams' Super Bowl contract has traded 13,065,216 contracts lifetime, the most of any top-eight team, ahead of San Francisco at 12,353,296 and Chicago at 11,111,112. Polymarket's 32 yes prices sum to 103.4%, a reminder that each team's contract trades in its own order book.

The same disagreement runs through the MVP market: Josh Allen leads at 30.5% on Kalshi and 32% on Polymarket, but on Joe Burrow the books do not even overlap — Kalshi prices him at 17.5% for MVP, Polymarket at 15%, with Kalshi's best bid above Polymarket's best ask. Two crowds, two answers, and a long season left to settle both.

items.title: Four Days Out: The House Looks Settled, the Senate Does Not
items.body:
Four Days Out: The House Looks Settled, the Senate Does Not

Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, and with four days left the prediction markets have split Congress in two. The House looks close to settled: Polymarket prices Democrats at 94% to win it and Kalshi at 92%. The Senate is the real contest, priced at 69% for Democrats on both exchanges.

The combinations tell the same story. Kalshi prices a Democratic sweep of both chambers at 67.5%, a Democratic House with a Republican Senate at 26.5%, and a Republican sweep at just 7.3%. Traders have put $21 million into election markets in the past 24 hours alone, according to DeFi Rate.

The Senate map runs through a handful of races. Democrats need a net gain of four seats, and DeFi Rate notes the 51st seat runs through Maine, where Democrat Troy Jackson is priced at 68%. The biggest move of the last seven days is Kansas, where the Democrat's chance jumped from 40% to 53%.

Texas moved the same way: the Democrat rose from 65% to 72% over the week, while in Alaska the Democrat eased from 76% to 69%. The single most likely Senate outcome is Democrats holding more than 52 seats, at 35%, and the most likely House outcome is 230 to 233 Democratic seats, at 16%.

The polls point the same way, just less far. RealClearPolling's generic congressional ballot average has Democrats ahead 51.4% to 43.2%, an 8.2-point lead. The markets have gone further than the polls. Whether that gap is foresight or enthusiasm is what Tuesday settles.

items.title: One Exchange Now Handles Three-Quarters of Everything
items.body:
One Exchange Now Handles Three-Quarters of Everything

Prediction markets traded $121.6 billion in contracts in the last 30 days, and one exchange handled almost all of it. DeFi Rate puts Kalshi at $91.7 billion over Sep. 30 to Oct. 29, a 75.6% share, up 53% on the 30 days before. Polymarket US was a distant second at $14.1 billion and 11.6%, with Polymarket's international exchange at $5.0 billion and 4.1%.

The dollars tell a second story. Those $121.6 billion in contracts were $29.2 billion in dollars actually paid, and $4.2 billion traded in the last 24 hours alone. Oct. 29 printed $4.08 billion across all venues and Oct. 28 printed $4.50 billion, while Sunday, Oct. 25 was the busiest day in the window at $7.14 billion — football weekends still set the calendar.

Sports explain the concentration. Sports took 68% of the dollars paid on single markets, $14.8 billion in 30 days, ahead of crypto at 26% and finance at 3%. The single most-traded market in the last 24 hours was Carolina vs. Green Bay on Kalshi at $40 million, followed by Shelton vs. Kym at $19 million.

The challengers are growing faster, just from far behind. DraftKings Predictions and Novig both rose 115% on the prior 30 days, to $4.1 billion and $3.0 billion, and Underdog Exchange was the fastest grower at 158%. September as a whole traded $79.6 billion, up 56% — the question now is whether anyone closes the gap on the leader, or whether scale itself becomes the moat.

items.title: The Market Is Watching Itself: Polymarket's Hunt for Insider Bets
items.body:
The Market Is Watching Itself: Polymarket's Hunt for Insider Bets

Four days before the November 3 midterms, Polymarket is investigating dozens of its own election bets. The platform runs 506 individual election markets, and its compliance team is examining trading that may have used information traders had a duty to protect. At least two cases have already been referred to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

The hunt is led by Shana Bautista, a former FBI official who joined Polymarket in June and now runs a 16-person intelligence and investigations team. Its surveillance system pulls gigabytes of data per user — social media, Federal Election Commission filings, banking partners, cryptocurrency records and statistical models — and processes hundreds of alerts a day. Concentrated trading bursts, multiple accounts behaving alike and shared device identifiers all trigger a closer look, and alerts that cross internal thresholds go straight to Bautista's phone.

The money at stake explains the effort. Combined midterm trading across Polymarket and Kalshi passed $220 million by mid-October. Polymarket's House control market has drawn $24 million with Democrats priced at 92%, its Senate market $9 million with Democrats at 66%, and its balance-of-power contracts price a Democratic sweep at 65% against just 8% for a Republican sweep. Texas leads the Senate battlegrounds at $7 million in volume, with Michigan and Maine at $3 million each.

Polymarket is not alone in policing itself. Kalshi banned and fined political candidates for betting on themselves in April and handed a lifetime ban to former Rep. George Santos in July; it has opened more than 150 investigations this year and sent over 20 cases to law enforcement. Polymarket itself had previously referred more than 100 cases across various markets to law enforcement.

That self-policing now carries the market's credibility. Election prices shape fundraising, media narratives and voter perceptions, so a price moved by private polling is not just a bad trade — it distorts the signal everyone else is reading. Bautista's warning is blunt: if you have information you have a duty to protect, do not trade on it — we will find you.

items.title: Washington Sues Back: The CFTC Now Has 10 States in Court
items.body:
Washington Sues Back: The CFTC Now Has 10 States in Court

The prediction market fight is no longer just platforms against states. The federal government sued Utah on Monday, and counting Utah, Washington now has 10 states in court for trying to keep federally regulated exchanges out. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission filed in federal court in Salt Lake City, less than a week after Utah moved first.

Utah Attorney General Derek Brown sued Kalshi and trading firm Susquehanna in state court on October 20, alleging Kalshi has offered gambling bets to residents since at least September 2024 and calling them indistinguishable from what a sportsbook sells. Utah bans gambling outright, and the state seeks to block Kalshi's sports, election and cultural markets and recover the fees it collected. Utah has already beaten Kalshi once: a federal judge ruled for the state in August, and the Tenth Circuit refused emergency relief while Kalshi appeals.

The CFTC's position is that event contracts count as swaps, a category federal commodities law leaves to federal regulators alone, and that letting each state step in would leave exchanges answering to 50 regulators nationwide. Its earlier suits cover Arizona, Connecticut, Illinois, New York, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Rhode Island, New Mexico and Kentucky. Judges have sided with Washington so far in Minnesota, Illinois and Arizona, including an October 2 Illinois ruling that the state likely cannot force Kalshi to get a sports wagering license.

Where Washington has not stepped in, the exchanges are suing themselves: Kalshi in Louisiana on October 23, Polymarket US in Louisiana and Ohio, and Nadex and Ludlow in Missouri, whose cease-and-desist letters also remain in play for Polymarket, Robinhood, Crypto.com, Novig and Underdog.

The appeals courts are split: Nevada won at the Ninth Circuit, the Sixth Circuit turned down Kalshi in Ohio and Tennessee, and New Jersey, which lost at the Third Circuit, has asked the Supreme Court to step in, with Kalshi's reply due November 9. Ten states in court, platforms suing in four more, and a Supreme Court petition pending: this is now a federal fight over who regulates the odds.

items.body:
Election Night Now Has a Ticker: The Odds Move Into the Newsroom

Four days before the November 3 midterms, prediction markets are no longer just a screen traders watch. They are moving into the newsroom itself. CNN, CBS News, CNBC and Dow Jones have entered commercial partnerships with Kalshi and Polymarket to cite election trading odds in their reporting, according to Bloomberg reporting on October 30.

The money explains the attention. Bloomberg analysis of Dune data puts election-related trading volume on Kalshi and Polymarket at about $1.5 billion. Traders are pricing Democrats at 94% to win the House on Polymarket and 69% to take the Senate, with Kalshi close behind at 92.1% for the House and 68.5% for the Senate.

The deals are not all the same. CBS News announced Kalshi as its prediction market sponsor. CNBC disclosed a partnership with Kalshi involving customer acquisition revenue sharing and a minority equity investment. The Wall Street Journal homepage now features a Polymarket odds column.

There are limits, and a debate. Fox and CNN said they will not broadcast odds on air on election night, and some commentators have raised concerns that commercial ties could compromise news independence. That tension is the story: the odds have become too large to ignore, and too commercial to treat as just another poll.

items.title: Prediction Markets Just Out-Earned Crypto at Robinhood
items.body:
Prediction Markets Just Out-Earned Crypto at Robinhood

The crossover is now official — and it is in the earnings. Robinhood reported third-quarter results on October 27, and event contracts generated $173 million in revenue, ahead of the $120 million from cryptocurrency trading, for the second straight quarter.

The volume behind it is enormous. Robinhood customers traded a record 16.4 billion event contracts in the quarter, up from 13.6 billion in the second quarter and more than seven times the year-earlier level. Prediction-market revenue rose 11% quarter over quarter, from $156 million, and more than sixfold year over year, inside record total revenue of $1.42 billion.

The mix is changing, too. Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma said non-sports contracts accounted for roughly 30% of prediction-market activity, up from about 15% in the prior quarter. Rothera, the prediction exchange Robinhood runs with Susquehanna, contributed $28 million and passed $100 million in annualized revenue in its first full quarter.

The exchanges supplying the market set their own records in October. Kalshi posted about $65 billion in volume, 10% above its September record, with open interest at a record $2.05 billion, while Polymarket US reached $10 billion, up roughly 15% from its previous monthly high.

Crypto revenue at Robinhood fell 55% from a year earlier. The forecast, it turns out, is now the bigger business.

Kalshi raised $1 billion at a $40 billion valuation on Thursday. It is also, at the same time, fighting for its legal life in courtrooms across America.

Utah has filed 14 criminal charges against Kalshi's co-founders. The CFTC has sued Utah right back, calling the charges federal overreach, and the CFTC's enforcement chief has named insider trading a top prediction-market priority.

The courts cannot agree with each other. State regulators have prevailed in Nevada, Maryland and Ohio — the Sixth Circuit recently ruled against Kalshi's federal preemption argument — while Kalshi won relief in Tennessee. Eleven states are pursuing legal action in total.

The market is adapting in real time. When Phantom rolled Kalshi markets into its wallet app this month, it blocked sports contracts in Michigan, and sports, elections and politics in Nevada and Washington.

There is now a market on whether the Supreme Court accepts a sports event contract case by December 31 — priced at 23.5%. The industry's future may be decided there.

items.body: - **CFTC asks Novig and ProphetX to hold off listing sports micro and scorigami contracts, CryptoWeek reports** — CryptoWeek reports the CFTC sent letters asking Novig and ProphetX not to list self-certified sports contracts and to explain why they comply with federal commodities law, with neither set yet listed for trading. Novig's micro contracts, such as which player scores the first points in a basketball game, were flagged as susceptible to manipulation, while ProphetX's scorigami contracts, which pay out on a final score never seen before in the sport, were said not to meet the Commodity Exchange Act definition of a swap, and ProphetX said it deferred listing and sent staff further analysis. items.title: CFTC rules split prediction markets from sportsbooks with event contracts as swaps and comments due November 18, CasinoJournal reports
items.body: - **CFTC rules split prediction markets from sportsbooks with event contracts as swaps and comments due November 18, CasinoJournal reports** — CasinoJournal reports two CFTC documents published in the Federal Register on Oct. 19 set out the split: sportsbook wagers and casino games are not swaps and belong to state and tribal regulators, while event contracts on sports, politics, culture and weather traded on federally registered exchanges are swaps under the CFTC. The interim exclusion took effect Oct. 19 and the proposed inclusion for 17 CFR 1.3 is not yet in force, with comments on both due Nov. 18. (CasinoJournal)

items.body: - **Nevada court issues 14-day restraining order barring Kalshi from offering sports, election and entertainment contracts in the state, GambleRss reports** — GambleRss reported Nevada's First Judicial District Court granted a 14-day temporary restraining order barring Kalshi from offering sports, election and entertainment event contracts in the state, the first time a state has forced a prediction market to halt operations. items.title: Federal judge blocks Minnesota prediction market ban, finding the law likely preempted by CFTC exclusive jurisdiction, GambleRss reports
items.body: - **Federal judge blocks Minnesota prediction market ban, finding the law likely preempted by CFTC exclusive jurisdiction, GambleRss reports** — GambleRss reported Judge Katherine Menendez issued a 44-page ruling granting preliminary injunctive relief to the CFTC, Kalshi and Polymarket US, concluding Minnesota's prediction market statute is likely at least partially preempted because the CFTC has exclusive jurisdiction over swaps traded on designated contract markets. The ruling found the platforms faced irreparable harm from possible criminal prosecution and substantial liability if trades had to be cancelled. (GambleRss)

items.title: CFTC is again probing whether Polymarket broke its 2022 settlement barring US users, Reuters reports
items.body: - **CFTC is again probing whether Polymarket broke its 2022 settlement barring US users, Reuters reports** — Reuters reports the CFTC is investigating whether Polymarket took sufficient steps to keep US users off its main overseas platform under a 2022 settlement, examining its location controls and US advertising as part of a broader probe opened earlier this year. The agency is also scrutinizing onboarding and customer protections on Polymarket's US platform, and both the CFTC and Polymarket declined to comment. (Reuters)

items.title: Kalshi bans three US candidates for five years for trading on their own races, BitRss reports
items.body: - **Kalshi bans three US candidates for five years for trading on their own races, BitRss reports** — Kalshi suspended Minnesota state senator Matt Klein, Texas congressional candidate Ezekiel Enriquez and Virginia Senate candidate Mark Moran after finding they traded on elections they were directly involved in, in violation of its CFTC-approved rule against trading by people who can influence an outcome. Klein was fined 539.85 dollars, Enriquez 784.20 dollars and Moran 6,229.30 dollars, and all three received five-year bans. (BitRss)

items.body: - **Polymarket trader beachboy4 loses 2.07 million dollars in 35 days despite a 51 percent win rate, BitRss reports** — A Polymarket trader known as beachboy4 lost more than 2.07 million dollars in 35 days across 53 prediction trades despite winning 51 percent of them, according to Coinpedia reporting shared by BitRss. The losses were attributed to average bets of about 400,000 dollars, frequent high-priced entries and no stop-loss or hedging, with a largest single loss of 1.58 million dollars against a largest win of about 936,000 dollars. (BitRss)

items.title: Canada limits regulated prediction markets to economic, environmental and financial contracts, BitcoinCasinos reports
items.body: - **Canada limits regulated prediction markets to economic, environmental and financial contracts, BitcoinCasinos reports** — Joint guidance from CIRO and the Canadian Securities Administrators allows authorized dealers to offer only event contracts tied to economic forecasts, environmental indicators and financial markets with a minimum 30-day maturity, while election and political contracts remain prohibited. Wealthsimple and Interactive Brokers Canada are the only CIRO dealers authorized to offer such contracts, and Wealthsimple Predict launched in July. (BitcoinCasinos)

items.title: Kalshi sues Louisiana to block enforcement of state gambling laws, iGaming Times reports

items.title: Polls show deadlock in Israel election but Kalshi and Polymarket strongly favour Eisenkot over Netanyahu, SA Jewish Report reports
items.body: - **Polls show deadlock in Israel election but Kalshi and Polymarket strongly favour Eisenkot over Netanyahu, SA Jewish Report reports** — SA Jewish Report, via JTA, reports Kalshi traders give Gadi Eisenkot a 52 percent chance of becoming Israel's next prime minister against 28 percent for Benjamin Netanyahu, while Polymarket puts Eisenkot at 58 percent and Netanyahu at 27 percent. Final polls put Eisenkot's change bloc at 52 to 56 seats and Netanyahu's coalition at about 50, with neither side holding a clear path to the 61 seats needed to govern. (SA Jewish Report)

items.title: NBA memorandum with CFTC creates no binding obligations as Kalshi and Polymarket become preferred exchanges, iGaming Times reports
items.body: - **NBA memorandum with CFTC creates no binding obligations as Kalshi and Polymarket become preferred exchanges, iGaming Times reports** — iGaming Times reports the NBA has named Kalshi and Polymarket its Preferred Prediction Market Exchanges and expanded its agreement with DraftKings to cover prediction markets, with the exchanges receiving NBA intellectual property, marketing rights and Sportradar data in return for market limits, a personnel trading ban and information-sharing duties. The league's memorandum of understanding with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission creates no legally binding obligations and leaves information sharing at each party's discretion. (iGaming Times)

The Commission alleges Kalshi has run a sports wagering business in New York for at least 18 months without a license, and the report notes the damages New York is seeking top 36 billion dollars according to the CFTC. (Gambling Insider)

items.body: - **Trump Jr.-backed 1789 Capital set to invest 300 million dollars in Polymarket in reported 1 billion dollar round at 21 billion dollar valuation, BitRss reports** — BitRss, citing a Wall Street Journal report, said 1789 Capital, where Donald Trump Jr. is a partner, is set to invest about 300 million dollars in Polymarket as part of a reported 1 billion dollar fundraising round that could value the platform at 21 billion dollars. The commitment would lift 1789 Capital's total disclosed exposure to Polymarket to about 500 million dollars, while ICE remains the largest disclosed investor with 1.6 billion dollars invested and about 22 percent of outstanding shares. (BitRss)

items.title: Senators Curtis and Schiff ask CFTC to investigate Polymarket over alleged deceptive influencer marketing, BitRss reports
items.body: - **Senators Curtis and Schiff ask CFTC to investigate Polymarket over alleged deceptive influencer marketing, BitRss reports** — Republican Senator John Curtis and Democratic Senator Adam Schiff wrote to CFTC Chair Mike Selig asking the agency to investigate Polymarket over allegations it paid social media influencers to promote fake bets without clear disclosure. The letter follows a Wall Street Journal review of more than 1,100 promotional videos that found 70 percent included fake bets totaling nearly 2 million dollars; Polymarket said it is auditing its promotional content for compliance. (BitRss)

items.title: Kentucky sues Kalshi and Polymarket over sports betting contracts and names Coinbase, Robinhood and Webull, BitRss reports
items.body: - **Kentucky sues Kalshi and Polymarket over sports betting contracts and names Coinbase, Robinhood and Webull, BitRss reports** — Kentucky filed lawsuits against five prediction market platforms including Kalshi and Polymarket, and also named Kalshi partners Coinbase, Robinhood and Webull, alleging the platforms are operating sports wagering in the state without required authorization. The complaints add to a broader set of state challenges arguing sports event contracts are unlicensed gambling, while the operators argue the products are swaps under CFTC jurisdiction. (BitRss)

items.title: Polymarket fortune-cookie ad with QR code goes viral and draws backlash, Softonic reports
items.body: - **Polymarket fortune-cookie ad with QR code goes viral and draws backlash, Softonic reports** — A fortune-cookie insert carrying a Polymarket promotion and a QR code drew millions of views and widespread criticism after researcher Jared Holt shared a photo of it on social platforms on October 26. It is not publicly confirmed whether Polymarket placed the ad itself or a third party handled it, and critics said a betting promotion inside a restaurant dessert normalizes gambling around children and people vulnerable to addiction. (Softonic)

items.title: Canada limits regulated prediction markets to economic, environmental and financial contracts, BitcoinCasinos reports
items.body: - **Canada limits regulated prediction markets to economic, environmental and financial contracts, BitcoinCasinos reports** — Under joint guidance from CIRO and the Canadian Securities Administrators issued August 27, authorized Canadian dealers may offer only event contracts tied to economic forecasts, environmental indicators and financial markets with a minimum 30-day maturity, while election and political contracts remain prohibited. Wealthsimple and Interactive Brokers Canada are the only CIRO dealer members authorized to offer such contracts. (BitcoinCasinos)

items.title: Brennan Center study finds prediction market odds sway voters by 10 to 20 points, Casino.org reports
items.body: - **Brennan Center study finds prediction market odds sway voters by 10 to 20 points, Casino.org reports** — A Brennan Center study of 1,994 registered voters conducted September 21 found a candidate favored by prediction markets gains a 10 to 20 percentage point boost in perceived victory regardless of polling, while low odds reduce perceived viability by 11 to 19 points. More than 80 percent of respondents favored stricter rules or bans on political event contracts. (Casino.org)

items.title: Kalshi sues Louisiana attorney general to block state gambling enforcement against its sports event contracts, SportsBettingDime reports
items.body: - **Kalshi sues Louisiana attorney general to block state gambling enforcement against its sports event contracts, SportsBettingDime reports** — Kalshi filed suit against Louisiana and Attorney General Liz Murrill seeking a temporary restraining order and preliminary and permanent injunctions, arguing the Commodity Exchange Act gives the CFTC exclusive jurisdiction over its event contracts. The complaint cites a state law that took effect August 1 expanding the definition of gambling by computer, a December 2025 Gaming Control Board advisory declaring such contracts illegal gambling, and public comments by Murrill describing the contracts as gambling. (SportsBettingDime)

items.body: - **Michigan attorney general asks court to hold Kalshi in contempt over targeted ads despite injunction, WeeBet reports** — Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel asked Ingham County Circuit Court Judge Rosemarie Aquilina to hold Kalshi in contempt, alleging the platform ran targeted ads at Michigan residents despite a preliminary injunction barring it from offering or marketing contracts in the state. items.body: - **NBA names Kalshi and Polymarket preferred prediction market exchanges and signs CFTC integrity pact, CDC Gaming reports** — The NBA on Monday designated Kalshi and Polymarket as its preferred prediction market exchanges and signed a memorandum of understanding with the CFTC. (CDC Gaming)

items.title: Polymarket and Kalshi pour over 5 million dollars into political campaigns amid regulatory scrutiny, Prediction News reports
items.body: - **Polymarket and Kalshi pour over 5 million dollars into political campaigns amid regulatory scrutiny, Prediction News reports** — Prediction News, citing a Reuters review of campaign finance disclosures published October 22, reported that Polymarket, Kalshi and their founders have given at least 5 million dollars combined to Republican and Democratic political campaigns and committees. The spending includes a previously unreported 1 million dollar Polymarket donation to a Democratic nonprofit that does not disclose its donors, while Polymarket and its CEO directed about 1.3 million dollars to Republican committees and candidates. (Prediction News)

items.title: Kalshi and Polymarket price Democrats at 68 percent for Senate control and about 90 percent for House control in October 23 midterm board, Prediction Markets Picks reports
items.body: - **Kalshi and Polymarket price Democrats at 68 percent for Senate control and about 90 percent for House control in October 23 midterm board, Prediction Markets Picks reports** — Prediction Markets Picks, in a board updated October 23 at 8:07 AM ET, showed Kalshi pricing Democrats at 68 percent to control the Senate and 90 percent to control the House, with Polymarket international at 68 cents for Senate control and 93 cents for House control. Its closest Senate races on Kalshi, by Democratic win probability, were Kansas at 38 percent and Iowa at 42 percent, with Maine at 63 percent, Texas at 66 percent, Ohio at 69 percent and Michigan at 69 percent. (Prediction Markets Picks)

items.title: Brewers favoured at about 62 percent over Rays in World Series markets on Polymarket and Kalshi, Action Network reports
items.body: - **Brewers favoured at about 62 percent over Rays in World Series markets on Polymarket and Kalshi, Action Network reports** — Action Network reported that with the World Series matchup set, Polymarket priced Tampa Bay at 37.6 percent to win the title and Kalshi at 38 percent, leaving Milwaukee favoured at roughly 62 percent on both platforms. Milwaukee finished with a 103-59 record, the best in the majors, and holds home-field advantage, while the Dodgers, who led at about 44 percent when four teams remained, are off the board. (Action Network)

items.title: Polymarket leads US prediction market search demand with 57.8 percent share despite Kalshi trading dominance, Gambling Insider reports
items.body: - **Polymarket leads US prediction market search demand with 57.8 percent share despite Kalshi trading dominance, Gambling Insider reports** — Gambling Insider, citing Blask data for January through August 2026, reported that Polymarket held 57.8 percent of branded prediction market search demand in the United States, down 16.56 points over the period, while Kalshi rose 12.7 points to 35.8 percent. The trading picture differed, with Kalshi recording 37.17 billion dollars in August volume against a combined 8.16 billion dollars across Polymarket and Polymarket US, according to The Block figures cited in the report. (Gambling Insider)

items.body: - **Thunder beat Nuggets 96-84 as largest trader reverses a 435,400 dollar position against Oklahoma City, Lines.com reports** — Lines.com reported Oklahoma City beat Denver 96-84 in the settled October 22 NBA prediction market, with the largest trader first placing 435,400 dollars against the Thunder and later buying 354,622 dollars on Oklahoma City as its probability rose. items.title: Utah attorney general seeks 61.2 million dollars from Kalshi over 3 billion dollars in trades by 32,000 residents, SCCG reports
items.body: - **Utah attorney general seeks 61.2 million dollars from Kalshi over 3 billion dollars in trades by 32,000 residents, SCCG reports** — SCCG reported on October 23 that Utah Attorney General Derek Brown filed a complaint against Kalshi, an affiliate and two Susquehanna trading firms, seeking up to 61.2 million dollars over about 3 billion dollars in trades by at least 32,000 Utah residents. Utah wants Kalshi sports, politics, election and culture contracts blocked in the state, while Kalshi argues its CFTC regulation preempts state gambling law, following an August federal ruling that rejected preemption for sports contracts. (SCCG)

items.title: New study of about one million contracts finds prediction markets highly calibrated across 12 domains, Marginal Revolution reports
items.body: - **New study of about one million contracts finds prediction markets highly calibrated across 12 domains, Marginal Revolution reports** — Marginal Revolution, summarizing a new PNAS paper published October 23, reports that researchers evaluated approximately one million resolved contracts and questions across Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold and Metaculus in 12 domains and found forecast probabilities were highly calibrated overall. items.title: CFTC enforcement chief says Maduro trading on his own capture would not necessarily break insider trading law, Covers reports
items.body: - **CFTC enforcement chief says Maduro trading on his own capture would not necessarily break insider trading law, Covers reports** — CFTC enforcement director Miller told the NEXTPredict summit that trading on the capture of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro would not necessarily have violated insider trading law, while noting a US service member was charged in April over bets linked to that operation. Miller said the CFTC has investigated several political candidates over election-related trading and that false statements made to move contract prices can count as market manipulation. (Covers)

Robins said the company does not offer sports event contracts in states where it holds a sportsbook licence, and that non-sports contracts have beaten expectations with a bigger push planned within months. (iGaming Express)

items.title: CFTC sues Illinois over state plan to regulate prediction markets, GambleRss reports
items.body: - **CFTC sues Illinois over state plan to regulate prediction markets, GambleRss reports** — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission sued Illinois in the US District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, arguing the Commodity Exchange Act gives it exclusive jurisdiction over designated contract markets and preempts state gaming rules, and asking the court to enjoin state enforcement. The suit, described as the first time the federal agency has sued a state over prediction market regulation, was filed a year and a day after Illinois issued cease-and-desist letters to Crypto.com, Kalshi and Robinhood, with a similar letter sent to Polymarket in January. (GambleRss)

items.title: Crypto.com and Novig exchanges sue Missouri over sports event contracts, BitcoinCasinos reports
items.body: - **Crypto.com and Novig exchanges sue Missouri over sports event contracts, BitcoinCasinos reports** — North American Derivatives Exchange, the CFTC-regulated exchange behind Crypto.com prediction markets, filed suit in the Western District of Missouri on October 16, and Ludlow Exchange, which does business as Novig, filed a companion suit in the Eastern District the same day, arguing the Commodity Exchange Act preempts Missouri gambling law. The suits answer September cease-and-desist letters to six operators that gave them 30 days to stop serving Missouri or obtain a state license, pay a 10 percent tax on adjusted gross revenue and pay license fees of up to 500,000 dollars. (BitcoinCasinos)

items.title: Prediction market pioneers question whether volume boom improves accuracy at NEXTPredict panel, NEXTPredict reports
items.body: - **Prediction market pioneers question whether volume boom improves accuracy at NEXTPredict panel, NEXTPredict reports** — At the final main-stage panel of Day 1 at NEXTPredict NYC on Thursday, Microsoft Research economist David Rothschild said modern prediction markets are heavily driven toward volume, which is not necessarily optimized toward accuracy. Robin Hanson, Emile Servan-Schreiber and Tobias Moskowitz debated whether beneficiaries should pay to subsidize more accurate markets, whether adding traders trades expertise for diversity, and whether AI forecasting could take over part of the forecasting role while markets remain popular for trading. (NEXTPredict)

items.body: - **CBO scores Stop Lawmakers From Predicting Act at under 500,000 dollars in penalties over 2027 to 2036, CBO reports** — The Congressional Budget Office estimates H.R. 9367, which would prohibit members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from trading prediction market contracts tied to government policy, government action or political outcomes, would increase civil penalty collections by less than 500,000 dollars over 2027 to 2036. items.body: - **Vanderbilt study finds Polymarket 67 percent accurate, Kalshi 78 percent and PredictIt 93 percent across 2,500 markets, BitRss reports** — Researchers Joshua Clinton and TzuFeng Huang at Vanderbilt University examined 2,500 markets with 2.5 billion dollars in volume across Polymarket, Kalshi and PredictIt and defined accuracy by how closely odds lined up with outcomes. items.title: CFTC splits prediction markets from sportsbook in paired rulemaking after circuit court split, Mavengity reports
items.body: - **CFTC splits prediction markets from sportsbook in paired rulemaking after circuit court split, Mavengity reports** — The CFTC interim final rule follows the Third Circuit approach in KalshiEX v. Flaherty, after the Sixth Circuit in September and the Ninth Circuit in August treated sports event contracts as indistinguishable from sports wagers. The rule says sports-related event contracts on a CFTC-licensed market can fit the definition of swaps, while using agency authority to exclude far-fetched scenarios as in the 2012 rulemaking. (Mavengity)

items.title: Missouri hits Polymarket and Kalshi with cease-and-desist orders, Bitcoin.com News reports
items.body: - **Missouri hits Polymarket and Kalshi with cease-and-desist orders, Bitcoin.com News reports** — Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway sent cease-and-desist letters to Polymarket, Kalshi, Crypto.com, Novig, Underdog and Robinhood, calling on them to stop offering sports event contracts to Missourians or face enforcement in 30 days. The state says the contracts dodge sports gambling rules, license fees and a 10 percent tax, and cannot be labeled event contracts to skirt compliance. (Bitcoin.com News)

items.title: NBER study finds no systematic political bias in election prediction market prices from 1880 to 2025

items.title: CFTC expands crypto and prediction-market rulemaking as fiscal 2025 enforcement actions fall 78%
items.body: - **CFTC expands crypto and prediction-market rulemaking as fiscal 2025 enforcement actions fall 78%** — The CFTC is advancing rulemaking for retail crypto transactions and prediction markets while its fiscal 2025 enforcement actions fell 78% to 13, down from 58 the prior year. items.body: - **Bipartisan Schiff-Curtis bill would ban sports event contracts on prediction markets** — Senators Adam Schiff and John Curtis are set to propose the first bipartisan bill restricting prediction-market platforms from offering sports event contracts, the Wall Street Journal reports. The bill would block CFTC-regulated platforms including Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood, Crypto.com and Coinbase from listing sports wagers and casino-style game markets; Kalshi called it a casino-backed push that would drive trading offshore. (GambleRss)

items.title: CFTC finalizes rule excluding casino-style gambling from swap definition
items.body: - **CFTC finalizes rule excluding casino-style gambling from swap definition** — The CFTC's interim final rule (RIN 3038-AF81), published October 9, states that casino-style gambling products are not swaps and fall outside its jurisdiction. Legal observers say the rule is aimed at protecting sports, politics and culture event contracts while undercutting recent court rulings in the Ninth and Sixth Circuits. (Deadspin)

items.title: CFTC moves to define event contracts as swaps, draws line at sportsbooks
items.body: - **CFTC moves to define event contracts as swaps, draws line at sportsbooks** — The CFTC announced two measures: one would formally classify event contracts linked to sports, politics, culture and weather as swaps, while an interim final rule explicitly excludes sportsbook wagers and casino games. Chairman Michael S. Selig said the products are commodity derivatives within the agency's exclusive jurisdiction. (World Casino Directory)

items.title: Canada's CIRO lets Wealthsimple offer prediction markets, bars sports and politics contracts
items.body: - **Canada's CIRO lets Wealthsimple offer prediction markets, bars sports and politics contracts** — The Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization approved Wealthsimple to offer prediction-market event contracts on economic forecasts, labor markets, housing and financial indicators. The approval explicitly excludes sports and political contracts, and other provinces may still decline to authorize access. (GambleRss)

items.title: Connecticut issues nine cease-and-desist orders against prediction-market operators
items.body: - **Connecticut issues nine cease-and-desist orders against prediction-market operators** — Connecticut Governor Ned Lamont announced nine cease-and-desist orders and 30 subpoenas against prediction-market platforms offering sports event contracts in the state. Recipients include Polymarket, Coinbase, Crypto.com, Robinhood, ProphetX, Novig, Webull, Gemini and Underdog, who face civil and criminal penalties if they continue. (GambleRss)

items.title: Polymarket and Kalshi founders launch 5c(c) Capital fund for prediction-market startups
items.body: - **Polymarket and Kalshi founders launch 5c(c) Capital fund for prediction-market startups** — Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan and Kalshi co-founder Tarek Mansour are launching 5c(c) Capital, a venture fund named after the Commodity Exchange Act section governing prediction markets. The fund targets up to $35 million across roughly 20 early-stage investments in data analytics, liquidity, and compliance startups built around prediction market infrastructure. (TokenPost)

items.title: Kalshi hires former FBI agent to lead anti-money-laundering efforts
items.body: - **Kalshi hires former FBI agent to lead anti-money-laundering efforts** — Kalshi has hired a former FBI agent to lead its anti-money-laundering efforts as regulatory scrutiny of the prediction-market industry intensifies alongside surging trading volumes. The move reflects growing compliance expectations for real-money platforms that now straddle financial-exchange and wagering categories. (Complete iGaming)

items.title: FCA confirms talks as Polymarket and Kalshi explore UK entry
items.body: - **FCA confirms talks as Polymarket and Kalshi explore UK entry** — The UK's Financial Conduct Authority has confirmed talks with Polymarket and Kalshi as both platforms explore entering the British market. A UK launch would require navigating both FCA rules on financial contracts and the Gambling Commission's stance on sports and political markets. (CCN)

items.title: Ninth Circuit ruling against Kalshi in Nevada brings Supreme Court fight closer
items.body: - **Ninth Circuit ruling against Kalshi in Nevada brings Supreme Court fight closer** — The Ninth Circuit unanimously ruled Friday that Nevada can enforce its gambling laws against Kalshi, rejecting the company's broad reading of the Commodity Exchange Act and clearing the way for states to restrict sports event contracts. The decision brings a Supreme Court fight over the industry's future one step closer. (GambleRss)

items.title: Baltimore sues Kalshi and Polymarket over alleged illegal sports betting
items.body: - **Baltimore sues Kalshi and Polymarket over alleged illegal sports betting** — Mayor Brandon Scott and the Baltimore City Council sued Kalshi and Polymarket on Thursday, alleging the platforms violate the city's consumer protection ordinance by operating unlicensed sports-betting platforms and misleading users about the legality of their event contracts. (GambleRss)

items.title: Connecticut judge says CFTC cannot override court's reading of federal law in Kalshi case
items.body: - **Connecticut judge says CFTC cannot override court's reading of federal law in Kalshi case** — U.S. District Judge Vernon D. Oliver ruled the CFTC cannot override his court's reading of federal law in Kalshi's Connecticut case, finding the agency's August market emergency order does not change his earlier conclusion that Kalshi's sports-event contracts are not swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act. The CFTC issued the order after New York Attorney General Letitia James sued Kalshi in state court; Connecticut's gaming laws stand. (GambleRss)

items.title: Kalshi seeks full 6th Circuit review of states' regulation win
items.body: - **Kalshi seeks full 6th Circuit review of states' regulation win** — Kalshi asked the full Sixth Circuit to review a three-judge panel ruling that Ohio and Tennessee can regulate it as unlicensed online sports gambling, arguing the panel erred and pointing to the CFTC's same-day proposals defining sports and other event contracts as federal swaps. The en banc petition, filed October 9, extends the industry's latest legal fight over whether state gambling laws reach federally registered prediction markets. (Bloomberg Law)

items.title: Kalshi targets pop culture fans as entertainment trading hits $813 million
items.body: - **Kalshi targets pop culture fans as entertainment trading hits $813 million** — Kalshi is pushing into entertainment contracts such as Dancing with the Stars and The Bachelor to court a wider audience: entertainment trading volume grew from $43 million in all of 2024 to $813 million so far in 2026, and the estimated share of female traders rose about 40% over the past year. Nearly $24 million was wagered on the winning Love Island couple, two-thirds of new users in that market were women, and the push is drawing familiar gambling-risk criticism. (MarketWatch)

items.title: 39 states, NFL, Dodd and Gensler file Supreme Court amicus briefs as CFTC moves to classify prediction contracts as swaps
items.body: - **39 states, NFL, Dodd and Gensler file Supreme Court amicus briefs as CFTC moves to classify prediction contracts as swaps** — Last week 39 states plus D.C., 145 tribal nations, the NFL, former Senator Chris Dodd and former CFTC chair Gary Gensler filed amicus briefs urging the Supreme Court to take up whether sports prediction contracts qualify as swaps, with most siding with state authority. On Friday the CFTC answered with an interim final rule and a new proposal explicitly classifying sports, political and other event contracts as federal swaps; Kalshi's deadline to respond was extended to November 9. (KuCoin)

items.title: NFL files amicus brief backing Supreme Court review of CFTC authority over prediction markets
items.body: - **NFL files amicus brief backing Supreme Court review of CFTC authority over prediction markets** — The NFL filed an amicus brief backing New Jersey's cert petition against Kalshi, asking the Supreme Court to clarify whether the CFTC has exclusive jurisdiction over sports event contracts. The league cites consumer harm, game-integrity risks and underage betting, while critics note the NFL has a financial interest in keeping prediction markets regulated like traditional sportsbooks. (Reason)

items.title: CFTC sues Wisconsin in fifth state lawsuit asserting jurisdiction over prediction markets
items.body: - **CFTC sues Wisconsin in fifth state lawsuit asserting jurisdiction over prediction markets** — The CFTC sued Wisconsin in federal court in the agency's fifth lawsuit against a US state over prediction-market jurisdiction, responding to the state's suits against Kalshi, Polymarket, Crypto.com, Robinhood and Coinbase. Chairman Michael Selig said states that interfere with federal oversight of the contracts will be sued, following similar actions against New York, Arizona, Connecticut and Illinois. (Cointelegraph)

items.title: Wisconsin judge rejects CFTC injunction bid against state prediction-market crackdown
items.body: - **Wisconsin judge rejects CFTC injunction bid against state prediction-market crackdown** — U.S. District Judge William C. Griesbach denied the CFTC's bid to block Wisconsin's enforcement against prediction-market platforms, ruling the agency showed neither irreparable harm nor a likelihood of success on the merits. The setback lands days after a Minnesota federal judge granted a preliminary injunction stopping a state ban, deepening the circuit split the Supreme Court is being asked to resolve. (SBC Americas)

items.title: CFTC issues no-action letter easing prediction-market data-reporting rules
items.body: - **CFTC issues no-action letter easing prediction-market data-reporting rules** — The CFTC issued a no-action letter easing data-reporting obligations for prediction markets, the latest in its push to cement exclusive federal jurisdiction over the sector. The move follows the agency's amicus brief in the Sixth Circuit arguing Ohio intruded on federally regulated markets, and its staff advisory classifying event contracts as a financial asset class. (Cointelegraph)

items.title: Kalshi and Polymarket hit all-time high with $50.6B combined July volume

The FIFA World Cup final between Spain and Argentina alone drew about $1.9 billion on Kalshi. (GambleRss)

items.title: Kalshi and Polymarket midterm markets face insider-trading scrutiny over knowable contracts
items.body: - **Kalshi and Polymarket midterm markets face insider-trading scrutiny over knowable contracts** — A new Anti-Corruption Data Collective analysis, first reported by CNN, flags the platforms' hyper-specific midterm election contracts as vulnerable to political insider trading, with more than $20 million in volume on so-called knowable markets. Researchers cited dozens of suspicious, correlated trades on a Kalshi contract about Graham Platner's Maine Senate withdrawal just before a damaging scandal became public. (Bonus (via CNN))

items.title: Reuters/Ipsos poll finds bipartisan opposition to election prediction markets
items.body: - **Reuters/Ipsos poll finds bipartisan opposition to election prediction markets** — A Reuters/Ipsos poll of 4,506 U.S. adults found bipartisan opposition to election betting on prediction markets, with 69% of Democrats and 61% of Republicans opposed. Opposition extends to betting on U.S. military actions (65%) and government policy announcements (63%) as regulators weigh oversight of the fast-growing platforms. (Traders Union (via Reuters/Ipsos))

The report notes the split between venues and the methodology behind the number remain unconfirmed, with prior scrutiny over how Kalshi's published volume statistics are constructed. (Coincu)

items.title: Prediction markets post record $188B Q3 volume as appeals court lets states restrict sports contracts
items.body: - **Prediction markets post record $188B Q3 volume as appeals court lets states restrict sports contracts** — Combined prediction-market volume hit a record $188B in Q3 2026, up nearly 70% quarter-over-quarter and 21x year-over-year, with Kalshi's sports trading driving the surge and permanently pulling ahead of Polymarket. A federal appeals court sided with Ohio and Tennessee on September 25, classifying the sports contracts as gambling and allowing states to restrict where Kalshi sells them. (Zubiqo)

items.title: Report: 69% of Polymarket retail accounts lose money; former Rep. Santos banned from Kalshi
items.body: - **Report: 69% of Polymarket retail accounts lose money; former Rep. Santos banned from Kalshi** — A Bradenton Herald report cited by Bonus.com found 69.2% of 2.9M Polymarket retail accounts finished below break-even, with $338.9M in total losses since 2020 and new research estimating 25% of historical volume is wash trading. The report also revealed up to 90% of Kalshi's bets are sports-related and that former Rep. George Santos was quietly issued a lifetime Kalshi ban after wagering on his own State of the Union attendance. (Bonus.com)

items.title: Kalshi sees $2B in 2026 election trades, eyes $10B+ on 2028 presidential election
items.body: - **Kalshi sees $2B in 2026 election trades, eyes $10B+ on 2028 presidential election** — Kalshi and Polymarket have handled $2 billion in U.S. election-based trades since the start of the year, RotoWire reports. Kalshi Politics head of growth Ben Freeman said on a media call that the platform could see upwards of $10 billion in trades on the 2028 presidential election, driven by rising institutional involvement from hedge funds, as Kalshi executives detailed new transparency and security protocols for midterm markets. (RotoWire)

The boom puts prediction markets on a direct collision course with traditional sportsbooks over how sports contracts should be treated and taxed. (Bloomberg Law)
